| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [orchestrator design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/05.orchestrator-design.md) |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-pm` SHALL accept `--session-suffix <lane>`, relocating its whole session directory to `.kiwi/sessions/{plan_run_id}/lanes/{lane}/`; `--no-final`, skipping T-final requirement promotion; and `--handoff <path>`, which supplies the execution set and the lease and nothing else — `kiwi-pm` executing exactly the front matter's `task_ids[]`, in sidecar declaration order, taking each Task's body from the sidecar path, using `write_set` as the commit pathspec, treating `req_ids[]` and `acceptance[]` as read-only context passed into the coder spawn prompt, treating a `depends_on_task` predecessor outside `task_ids[]` as satisfied, and refusing `--from-task` together with `--handoff`.

#### Rationale

Defining `--handoff` as the execution set and the lease is what makes it buildable: the handoff is not a plan and carries no Task bodies, no TDD block, no acceptance tests, no definition of done and no rollback, so a definition that called it the input source of truth left an implementer nothing to build from and left `kiwi-pm` executing every task of the plan in declaration order with only a start-point selector available — which would put two units over one plan each writing every file in it and each breaching its lease. `task_ids[]` is generally non-contiguous because it is a connected component of the conflict graph, which is precisely why a start-point selector cannot express it. `--session-suffix` restores per-unit ownership of `pm-state.json`, `pm.lock`, `worklog.jsonl`, `state.json` and the reports directory, discharging rather than weakening the sequential-spawn precondition that pm's own race-freedom rests on. From `05` §5.4.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `--handoff <path>` supplies the execution set and the lease and never the Task bodies: `kiwi-pm` executes exactly the front matter's `task_ids[]` and no other task of the plan, in sidecar declaration order, taking each Task's body from the sidecar path as it does today.
- [x] AC-2: `write_set` is the commit pathspec used by the commit flag, and `req_ids[]` and `acceptance[]` are read-only context passed into the coder spawn prompt that drive no execution decision.
- [x] AC-3: A `depends_on_task` predecessor outside `task_ids[]` is treated as satisfied and the depends-on-violation gate does not fire on it, while a dependency violation inside the execution set is still a gate.
- [x] AC-4: `--from-task` is refused together with `--handoff`, and the skill body records the reason: a start-point selector cannot express a generally non-contiguous `task_ids[]`.
- [x] AC-5: `--session-suffix <lane>` moves the whole session directory — `pm-state.json`, `pm.lock`, `worklog.jsonl`, `state.json` and the reports directory — to `.kiwi/sessions/{plan_run_id}/lanes/{lane}/`, and the run-id line in the coder spawn prompt from which `kiwi-coder` derives its own state paths follows the relocation.
- [x] AC-6: `--no-final` skips T-final requirement promotion, with the recorded reason that a requirement spans units and its all-done denominator would otherwise be one unit's task subset.
- [x] AC-7: The skill body does not define `--handoff` as `kiwi-pm`'s input source of truth: the execution-set-and-lease semantics above are what is written, so two units over one plan cannot each execute every task.
- [x] AC-8: The verification evidence for this requirement records an explicit runtime-lag note naming the installed path that still holds the old text — `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-pm/SKILL.md`, which carries none of the three flags — because `00.charter.md:303-304` forbids a reinstall against this repository.

### FR-FLOW-114 — kiwi-pm and kiwi-review-fix-loop accept no-pipeline-emit so a delegated unit writes no false pipeline record

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.6.0-phase1-kiwi-orchestrator |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [orchestrator design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/05.orchestrator-design.md), [scope and frame decisions](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/08.scope-and-frame-decisions.md) |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-pm` and `kiwi-review-fix-loop` — and not `kiwi-pipeline`, which no orchestrated unit invokes — SHALL accept `--no-pipeline-emit`, taking no argument and suppressing the append to `kiwi/pipeline.jsonl`, so that a unit executed under the orchestrator writes no pipeline record of its own.

#### Rationale

A child skill that appends its own pipeline event while running as one unit of a larger run writes a record that misdescribes the run: the pipeline journal would show a `kiwi-pm` run completing where in fact one unit of one stage of one wave completed, and a parent may not record on a child's behalf to correct it. Suppressing the child's append is therefore the only clean mechanism. The flag is registered on exactly the two skills a unit runs and deliberately not on `kiwi-pipeline`, which no unit invokes — an earlier revision named `kiwi-pipeline` here while the sections it cites named `kiwi-pm`, and a registration list whose purpose is to catch silent breakage is the worst place for that disagreement to sit. From `05` §14 registration 11 and §5.14.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `--no-pipeline-emit` is documented in both `kiwi-pm` and `kiwi-review-fix-loop` in all three variants and takes no argument.
- [x] AC-2: With the flag present neither skill appends to `kiwi/pipeline.jsonl`; without it, each skill's existing emit behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] AC-3: `kiwi-pipeline` does not gain the flag, and the recorded reason is that no orchestrated unit invokes it.
- [x] AC-4: The orchestrator's executor invocation passes `--no-pipeline-emit` on every unit run, and the body states the consequence of omitting it: the unit writes a false pipeline record.
- [x] AC-5: The verification evidence for this requirement records an explicit runtime-lag note naming the installed paths that still hold the old text — `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-pm/SKILL.md` and `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-review-fix-loop/SKILL.md`, neither of which documents the flag — because `00.charter.md:303-304` forbids a reinstall against this repository.

### FR-FLOW-115 — kiwi-pm accepts commit-lane-work so an orchestrated unit's work is committed with only its write set staged

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.6.0-phase1-kiwi-orchestrator |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [orchestrator design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/05.orchestrator-design.md), [scope and frame decisions](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/08.scope-and-frame-decisions.md) |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-pm` SHALL accept `--commit-lane-work`, taking no argument, committing each completed Task with only the `write_set` of the handoff already passed via `--handoff` staged and with the run's commit-policy trailers attached.

#### Rationale

Without the flag `kiwi-pm` commits nothing, so the rule that the work is written where it will live would leave a unit's output as an uncommitted working tree that the next unit's run then trips over; and because the commit range on the integration branch is what the orchestrator derives its record from in this target, an uncommitted unit is an unrecorded one. The flag takes no argument deliberately: an earlier revision typed it as taking a pathspec file and pointed that file at a path under the orchestrator's own state directory, which is git-ignored and therefore absent from an isolated workspace, so the pathspec has to come from the handoff the same invocation already names. From `05` §14 registration 11, §5.14 difference 4 and §10.5 step 9.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `--commit-lane-work` is documented on `kiwi-pm` in all three variants, takes no argument, and stages exactly the `write_set` of the handoff already passed via `--handoff`.
- [x] AC-2: One commit is produced per completed Task, staging an explicit pathspec drawn from `write_set` and never staging the whole working tree.
- [x] AC-3: Each commit carries the run coordinates in git trailers and no run coordinate in the commit subject.
- [x] AC-4: The skill body records that a pathspec file is deliberately not used, because any path under the orchestrator's own state directory is git-ignored and therefore absent from an isolated workspace.
- [x] AC-5: The body states the consequence of omitting the flag: `kiwi-pm` commits nothing and the unit's output is left as an uncommitted working tree the next unit trips over.
- [x] AC-6: `--commit-lane-work` is documented on `kiwi-pm` and is not documented on `kiwi-review-fix-loop` in this target.
- [x] AC-7: The verification evidence for this requirement records an explicit runtime-lag note naming the installed path that still holds the old text — `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-pm/SKILL.md`, which does not document the flag — because `00.charter.md:303-304` forbids a reinstall against this repository.

### FR-FLOW-116 — kiwi-tdd declares a critical gates table and joins the closed pipeline skill enum

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.6.0-phase1-kiwi-orchestrator |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [routing design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/09.routing-design.md), [orchestrator design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/05.orchestrator-design.md) |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-tdd` SHALL declare a `critical_gates[]` table in the three-column `gate_id | reason | location` form, and `_shared/kiwi/pipeline-event.md` SHALL add `kiwi-tdd` to its closed `skill` enum with a T1 routing-hint row.

#### Rationale

`kiwi-tdd` declares no `critical_gates[]` today, and by the shared safe default that makes `--auto` inactive for it — a silent ignore rather than a failure, so the skill runs but still stops at its own user gates, which under an unattended run is a stall no automatic mechanism can clear. It is also absent from the closed pipeline `skill` enum, so its events are warned about and skipped, which means a delegated step run leaves the orchestrator's own event as the only journal record and a parent may not record on the child's behalf to fill the hole. This is authored as a separate additive requirement rather than folded into the routing requirements, because folding it in would smuggle a second behavioural change into them. From `09` §4.4, §5.1, §13 A4 and A7, and `05` §14 registration 3-prime.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `kiwi-tdd/SKILL.md` carries a `critical_gates[]` table in the three-column `gate_id | reason | location` form in all three variants; the string does not occur in the skill today.
- [x] AC-2: Each of the four user-interaction points that survive a correctly dispatched step run — the Phase 1 claim write-skew rejection, the Architecture-Decisions approval, `EVIDENCE_REQUIRED` on promote, and the Phase 7 completion gate — appears in the skill body with a stated severity, so none of them falls to the undeclared-gate default.
- [x] AC-3: With the table declared, `--auto` is no longer inactive for `kiwi-tdd` by the shared safe default, and the skill body states which of its gates `--auto` can and cannot resolve.
- [x] AC-4: `kiwi-tdd` is a member of `pipeline-event.md`'s closed `skill` enum in all four shipped copies, so its events are no longer warned about and skipped as out-of-enum.
- [x] AC-5: `pipeline-event.md`'s T1 table gains a `kiwi-tdd` row.
- [x] AC-6: This requirement is authored separately from the routing requirements and none of them depends on it: until it lands, a delegated step run leaves the orchestrator's own event as the only journal record, which the routing design states rather than working around by having the parent record on the child's behalf.
- [x] AC-7: The verification evidence for this requirement records an explicit runtime-lag note naming the installed paths that still hold the old text — `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-tdd/SKILL.md`, which declares no critical gates table, and `~/.claude/skills/_shared/kiwi/pipeline-event.md`, whose skill enum lacks the entry — because `00.charter.md:303-304` forbids a reinstall against this repository.

#### Verification Evidence

AC-1 runs it.each over the four shipped kiwi-tdd renderings, asserts a critical_gates section exists, that its header splits into exactly three content columns, and that they are gate_id, a reason and a location. AC-2 asserts each of the three critical gate ids is its own table row with a non-empty reason and a non-empty location, that the parsed gate-id set equals the canonical three and is identical across the four copies, that no gate is declared twice, that each row names the phase it fires in, and that the fourth surviving interaction point sds-architecture-decision-approval carries the explicit severity business-decision while being absent from the critical table. AC-3 asserts the gate section mentions --auto, carries a line naming what --auto cannot resolve and a line naming what it can, and names the superseded safe default so the change is legible. ### FR-FLOW-117 — kiwi-pipeline section 2.8 accepts a frozen route lock as its step-scoped conjunct

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.6.0-phase1-kiwi-orchestrator |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [routing design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/09.routing-design.md), [orchestrator design](../research/kiwi-orchestrator/05.orchestrator-design.md) |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-pipeline` section 2.8 SHALL state that when a `kiwi-orchestrator` run has frozen a route, section 2.8's step-scoped conjunct is satisfied by `route.lock.json` and is not re-judged.

#### Rationale

Section 2.8 routes on a conjunction of work-mode and step-scope, but only the first conjunct is operational: step-scope is given no test, no threshold and no named input anywhere in that section or in the shared work-mode policy. The routing classifier's disqualifier set is that missing definition, so the amendment records where the conjunct is now answered rather than leaving two places to answer it. It is needed even though section 2.8 never runs inside an orchestrator run today — cycle and from-stage entries are excluded from its routing and the orchestrator calls the stages individually — precisely so that a later change to that exclusion does not silently create two live routers disagreeing mid-run. From `09` §4.1 and §11, and `05` §14 registration 8.

- [x] AC-2: The amendment changes nothing about section 2.8 outside an orchestrator run: the work-mode conjunct and the fallback chain for work that is not step-scoped are unchanged.
- [x] AC-3: The body records why the amendment exists although section 2.8 never runs inside an orchestrator run today — cycle and from-stage entries are excluded from its routing and the orchestrator calls the stages individually — so that a later change to that exclusion does not silently create two live routers.
- [x] AC-4: The body records that the step-scoped conjunct section 2.8 declares and never defines is supplied by the classifier's disqualifier set, and that the definition only ever narrows the step rung and never widens it.
- [x] AC-5: The verification evidence for this requirement records an explicit runtime-lag note naming the installed path that still holds the old text — `~/.claude/skills/kiwi-pipeline/SKILL.md`, whose section 2.8 carries no such sentence — because `00.charter.md:303-304` forbids a reinstall against this repository.

### FR-FLOW-118 — The run contract's closed list of forbidden actions has a fixed membership

#### Requirement

The closed list of forbidden actions the kiwi-orchestrator skill body states SHALL have a fixed membership of exactly eight prohibitions — no re-decomposition, no Requirement ID allocation outside Phase 3.b, no editing a completed unit, no weakening or deleting tests, no writing outside the lease, no hand-appending to the run journal, no git add -A or git commit -a, and no merging the integration branch into the base branch or opening a pull request — stated identically in all three shipped variants, and the deletion of any one of them SHALL be a test failure.

#### Rationale

FR-FLOW-093 names the list and pins two of its eight entries: AC-3 the merge and pull-request pair, AC-5 the bulk-staging pair. Nothing fixed the other four, and a grep over test/ for the list or its heading returned nothing, so five of the eight could have been deleted from a shipped skill with every gate staying green. A list that calls itself closed while its membership is unasserted is closed in name only. The mutation ledger landed on 2026-08-02 already pins all eight with one rule each and a red mutation apiece; this requirement records the obligation the ledger discharges, so the membership does not depend on a test nobody's requirement asks for. Measured: the list is one line in each variant, byte-identical across the three.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: All eight prohibitions appear in the closed list in each of the three shipped variants, and the list is the same in all three.
- [x] AC-2: Deleting any one of the eight from a variant fails a named test, so the closed list cannot shrink silently.
- [x] AC-3: The assertion enumerates the eight from a declared set rather than from a count literal, so adding a ninth prohibition without declaring it also fails.
- [x] AC-4: The requirement's Verification Evidence records the runtime-lag note naming the installed copy that still holds the pre-change text, because the charter forbids running speckiwi init, speckiwi skills install or speckiwi upgrade --apply against this repository.

### FR-FLOW-119 — --drive autonomous wave mode: bounded self-repair behind a closed refusal list

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | v2.4.4 |
| Status | implemented |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | wave-master, auto, drive, unattended, gates |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

When the user passes `--drive`, kiwi-wave-master SHALL carry the whole wave sequence to the last wave without user interaction: it SHALL imply `--auto`, `--auto-integration` and `--auto-cost-warning`; it SHALL authorise self-repair of a blocking defect only when the repair is reversible, confined to the run root, leaves existing public contracts and existing tests unchanged, and rests on a diagnosis reproduced by an independent check; it SHALL NOT open the gates named in its refusal list, whatever confidence a committee reports; and it SHALL name in the wave journal every gate it resolves automatically and every gate it halts on.

#### Rationale

Measured on a real run (DocuOrbit, 2026-08-02, kiwi/waves.jsonl). The installed kiwi-wave-master declared no critical_gates[], which auto-option.md defines as `--auto` inactive with silent ignore, so `--auto` had been a no-op and every wave boundary asked the user to continue. The Wave 5 halt is the second half of the evidence: the agent reproduced the cause independently (a JDK 8 tools.jar absent from the test compile classpath), proposed a reversible one-line build fix, judged it the recommended path, and halted anyway; that journal line records the stop in prose and names no gate, so the halt is traceable to no declared entry. FR-FLOW-059 already names that class of undeclared stop. The refusal list is the load-bearing half of the flag rather than a caveat on it: opening existing-test-weakened-or-deleted, existing-public-contract-change or out-of-scope-user-consent would let an unattended run reach green by weakening a test or by dropping a design item out of every denominator, so the run would finish while the goal shrank. That failure looks like success and happens where nobody is watching.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: All three shipped kiwi-wave-master variants give `--drive` its own section and state, in a sentence a test pins verbatim, that it turns on `--auto`, `--auto-integration` and `--auto-cost-warning` together.
- [x] AC-2: All three variants state the four self-repair conditions — reversible, confined to the run root, existing public contracts and existing tests unchanged, and a diagnosis reproduced by an independent check — as a conjunction whose failure halts, each condition in its own numbered item, with no hedge downgrading one to best-effort.
- [x] AC-3: All three variants declare a closed refusal list naming at least external-module-impact, existing-test-weakened-or-deleted, existing-public-contract-change, existing-file-deleted-or-moved, mock-detection, tdd-bypass-attempt, out-of-scope-user-consent, unsafe-option-refused and wave-append-cap-exhausted, state in a pinned sentence that `--drive` does not open them whatever confidence a committee reports, and carry no exception clause admitting one.
- [x] AC-4: All three variants state in a pinned sentence that wave-verify-residual-critical, final-verify-residual-critical and wave-verify-fail-residual stay closed under `--drive`, because reaching them means the automatic remediation loop already failed.
- [x] AC-5: `--drive` reaches its destination: the kiwi-wave-master pass-through table carries the row to kiwi-coder, kiwi-pipeline and kiwi-pm each state that they forward it, and kiwi-coder itself states that `--drive` opens its integration-test and cost-warning gates — without that last hop the route ends at a skill that has no rule for the token and the run halts there.
- [x] AC-6: All three variants state that a `--drive` halt names its gate id in the journal `abort_gate` field when that gate belongs to the orchestrator gate vocabulary, that a gate owned by a child skill arrives instead as child-pipeline-needs-user-or-failed, and that an automatically resolved gate records a `decision` row naming it.
- [x] AC-7: All four shipped copies of the shared `--auto` SSOT `_shared/kiwi/auto-option.md` record that one explicitly named flag may imply the child gate options, so the skill text does not contradict that module's rule that a parent never synthesises a child's gate-bypassing options.
- [x] AC-8: The critical-gate rows for integration-test-user-consent and cost-warning-large-task name `--drive` as an opener in all three variants, so the machine-read gate interface agrees with the prose rather than still halting the mode it declares.
- [x] AC-9: Every enumeration touching the forwarded option set names `--drive`: the kiwi-wave-master frontmatter, the kiwi-pm CLI argument summary and its pass-through paragraph, and the `decision` field occasions in the four waves-event copies. The kiwi-orchestrator inherited-option list names it as deliberately NOT inherited, because that skill runs its own gate table and its own `--auto` contract, so inheriting an implication set would claim it opens gates that table never declares.
- [ ] AC-10: An automated test pins each normative sentence above so that inverting it, hedging it, or adding an exception clause fails the suite — not only deleting its vocabulary — and scopes every section-bound assertion to a heading it cannot silently re-anchor away from.

### FR-FLOW-120 — The prickly review checks comment claims a machine can check

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.7.0-verification-integrity |
| Status | implemented |
| Priority | medium |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The prickly-review axis table in each bundled `kiwi-coder` variant SHALL declare an axis whose subject is the truth of a claim a code comment makes about the code, SHALL bound that axis to a closed set of claim kinds a machine can check without reading intent, SHALL state that a comment claim outside that set is not a finding, and SHALL leave the existing `@req` tag prohibition in force.

#### Rationale

The seven axes are intent preservation, security, edge cases, concurrency, refactoring scope, error handling and test quality. None asks whether a comment says something true, and one comment class — the `@req` tag — is explicitly exempted from being checked at all. So a comment asserting a fact about the code is never re-read against the code, which is the failure mode this target exists to close: measured in this repository's own SRS, prose asserted a fact, reality moved, and nothing re-read the assertion until 44 verified rows carried it. Code comments have the identical shape. The axis must be bounded because checking an arbitrary comment against code costs the same reasoning as judging an acceptance criterion — measured at roughly 27 seconds per requirement — which does not scale to every comment in a diff. Claims naming a path, a symbol, a count or an absence are decidable by existsSync and grep, so bounding the axis to those makes it nearly free while covering the claims that actually went false here.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Each of the three bundled `kiwi-coder` variants declares an axis in its prickly-review axis table whose stated subject is whether a comment's claim about the code holds, distinct from the refactoring axis whose subject is duplication, over-abstraction, naming and function size.
- [x] AC-2: That axis names a closed set of checkable claim kinds — a file or directory path, a code symbol name, a count, and an absence claim such as `no caller` or `not wired` — the set is stated as closed rather than as examples, and it is identical in all three variants.
- [x] AC-3: That axis states that a comment claim outside the closed set is not a finding, so the axis cannot expand into judging intent.
- [ ] AC-4: The existing prohibition on verifying `@req` tags is present and unweakened in all three variants after the change, and the closed set's symbol kind is qualified so that a REQ-ID cannot be read into it.
- [x] AC-5: The axis table's row count and the set of axis subjects are equal across the three variants, so no variant carries an axis another lacks.
- [ ] AC-6: Every count claim the skill makes about its own axis table agrees with the table: no rendering, and no other bundled skill that borrows the table by name, states a number that the table contradicts.
- [ ] AC-7: A comment claim in the closed set that is measurably false is routed to a severity the Phase 2 gate blocks on, so an axis finding can stop the pipeline rather than only being advised; comment style and wording remain at the lower severity.
- [x] AC-8: The `.agents` mirror of the changed skill carries the same axis table as its source variant, asserted by a test rather than by a manual sync step.

The denylist cases could not be finished — the Implementation Note records why — so four cells are pinned by canonical equality across all four copies instead: the axis row, the bounding sentence, and both severity lines. Mutation-measured: 16 single-copy rewordings all die; a COORDINATED reword of all four copies, and an additive clause that re-opens the bound while leaving every asserted phrase in place, pass every pre-existing assertion and die only on the pin. An independent audit then measured three further mutants surviving — a count claim written inside section 5.2 on a line naming neither scan token, a Phase 2 gate that stops blocking on HIGH, and a sentence exempting axis 8 from the `@req` prohibition — and all three now die. NOT closed and not claimed: `skills/etc` runs a different loop and its Phase 2 gate names no severity at all, so AC-7's stated mechanism is absent there; its gate line is pinned separately rather than rewritten. |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-coder` SHALL accept `--defer-srs-mutation <path>` and, under it, SHALL record each of its four mandatory MCP mutations to the queue at that path instead of calling them, keeping the queue entry shape and `args_hash` dedupe it already declares. `kiwi-pm` SHALL accept the same flag and pass it through into its `kiwi-coder` spawn prompt. The two halves SHALL be documented together in every shipped rendering — the three skill variants and the `.agents` mirror — because either half alone is inert: `kiwi-pm` owns the spawn, so a flag only `kiwi-coder` knows is unreachable, and a flag only `kiwi-pm` forwards is discarded by a `kiwi-coder` that does not read it.

#### Rationale

Charter C1 forbids SRS mutation inside a parallel task, but `kiwi-coder` §0.12 makes four MCP mutations mandatory per Task, and a lane's MCP writes land at the host root rather than in its worktree. Recording them to the existing `mcp_call_log[]` queue with the existing `args_hash` dedupe is the design's answer (05 §15.3 S12, §14 items 11-12, §5.4): the mutations are deferred, not skipped, because skipping them would break traceability while calling them would break C1. The design also states the two halves are inert apart, which is why one requirement owns both. No replay consumer exists yet — the queue producer lands first and the host-root replayer is separate work in this target.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Each of the four shipped `kiwi-coder` renderings — `skills/{claude,codex,etc}` plus the `.agents/skills` mirror — documents `--defer-srs-mutation <path>` in the §1.2 optional-input table and defines it in the §6.2 section its variant makes SSOT.
- [x] AC-2: Each of the four `kiwi-coder` renderings states — in whichever file that variant makes SSOT for §6.2, inline for the claude variant and `references/extended-workflow.md` for the others — that under the flag the four mandatory mutations are recorded to the queue rather than called, keeping the existing entry shape and `args_hash` dedupe; the rule sentence is asserted on its own, not on the sub-block heading that repeats its words, and the resolved SSOT section is asserted non-empty so a relocated section cannot pass by absence.
- [x] AC-3: Each of the four `kiwi-coder` renderings states, in sentences of their own, that the four mutations remain accounted for, that the orchestrator replays them at the host root, and that the flag is reached only through the `kiwi-pm` spawn rather than by direct invocation.
- [x] AC-4: Each of the four shipped `kiwi-pm` renderings documents `--defer-srs-mutation <path>` in all three places its sibling delegation flags occupy — the §1.2 optional-input table, the CLI argument summary, and the §1.5 delegation section — the §1.5 entry defines it as a pass-through into the `kiwi-coder` spawn prompt, and the §1.5 prose flag count agrees with the number its heading lists, so a member cannot be added to one and not the other.
- [x] AC-5: The flag carries a required path placeholder in every rendering of both skills, and no rendering names a default queue path — unlike `--commit-lane-work`, which takes no argument — so two lanes cannot be documented into sharing one queue.
- [x] AC-6: Each of the four `kiwi-coder` renderings states, in the shipped text a reader reaches rather than only in this requirement, the CONDITION under which the four queued mutations are lost — outside an orchestrator run that harvests AND applies the queue — absolutely rather than hedged, and names what is lost. That caveat is what makes the deferral in AC-2 safe to offer: the flag trades a direct mutation for a queued one, and a reader who does not know the queue must be harvested loses the traceability AC-2 preserves. No rendering may claim the applying consumer is absent, in any spelling that claim has taken: IR-CLI-091 landed the planner `orchestrate replay plan` and IR-CLI-092 landed the applier `orchestrate replay apply`, bound in `ORCHESTRATE_TOOL_BINDINGS` and backed by `applyReplayPlan`, so every form of the absence claim is now false and a criterion demanding one would pin a false sentence into four shipped renderings. This criterion keys on the condition rather than on a component's presence because a condition does not go stale when a component ships — keying on presence is what forced the earlier re-anchoring when the planner arrived. The superseded wording is refused by name as well, so a rendering cannot satisfy this by keeping the old absence sentence and adding the condition beside it.
- [x] AC-7: Each of the four `kiwi-coder` renderings states that `--dry-run` and `--defer-srs-mutation` are mutually exclusive and that the combination is refused with a recorded reason, rather than leaving a queue of `dry_run: true` entries whose replay semantics are undefined.

### FR-FLOW-122 — Shared worktree-lane contract that both orchestrating skills declare

| Field | Value |

| Priority | high |

| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/research/16.wave-master-per-wave-worktree-subagent-research.md |

#### Requirement

A shared contract document `_shared/kiwi/worktree-lane.md` SHALL be the single source of truth for how a run creates a git worktree and works inside it, and both `kiwi-orchestrator` and `kiwi-wave-master` SHALL declare it in their §0 rather than each restating the procedure. The contract SHALL separate the run root, which stays bound to the MCP workspace and owns every SRS mutation, from a lane workspace, which is a worktree that holds only code and test edits; SHALL require an explicit checkout of the intended base commit because a freshly created worktree does not open at the current branch; SHALL forbid a lane from calling an SRS mutation, from committing under `docs/spec/`, and from passing `--root`; SHALL state that deferred mutations are replayed at the host root through the admitted set only; SHALL state that a lane's own verification result is not the verdict, which the host obtains by running the verification command against the lane workspace itself; and SHALL state that the bootstrap install passes `--include=dev` so a `NODE_ENV=production` environment cannot silently omit devDependencies.

#### Rationale

Both skills need the same procedure and neither has it. Writing it twice would put one responsibility in two places, which is the failure this repository has already paid for elsewhere: one copy gets corrected and the other silently diverges. The specific facts the contract fixes are each measured rather than assumed — a runtime-created worktree opened at `origin/<default-branch>`, 114 commits behind the branch under work, so an implicit baseline is wrong; `npm ci` under `NODE_ENV=production` omits devDependencies and still exits 0, so a lane can report green from a toolchain that never ran the tests; and the MCP workspace root cannot follow a session into a worktree, so a lane that calls an SRS mutation writes to the host root and splits the run's own accounting.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `_shared/kiwi/worktree-lane.md` exists in every shipped skill bundle and carries a version marker.
- [x] AC-2: It distinguishes the run root from a lane workspace and states that every SRS mutation belongs to the run root.
- [x] AC-3: It requires an explicit checkout of the base commit and says why a created worktree's default head cannot be relied on.
- [x] AC-4: It forbids a lane from calling an SRS mutation, from committing anything under `docs/spec/`, and from passing `--root`.
- [x] AC-5: It states that deferred mutations are replayed at the host root and only for the admitted mutation set.
- [x] AC-6: It states that the host, not the lane, obtains the verification verdict by running the command against the lane workspace.
- [x] AC-7: It requires `--include=dev` on the bootstrap install and names the `NODE_ENV=production` failure it prevents.
- [x] AC-8: `kiwi-orchestrator` and `kiwi-wave-master` each declare the contract in their §0 table in every shipped rendering, and neither restates the procedure in place of referencing it.
- [x] AC-9: Adding this contract introduces neither `branch-serial-lane` nor `patch-lane` into either skill body, so the phase-1 profile assertions of FR-FLOW-088 stay green.

### FR-FLOW-123 — Both orchestrating skills carry an executable worktree procedure

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.6.0-phase2-parallel-lanes |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | orchestrator, wave-master, worktree, lane, skills |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/research/16.wave-master-per-wave-worktree-subagent-research.md |

#### Requirement

`kiwi-orchestrator` and `kiwi-wave-master` SHALL each carry a numbered section that an agent can execute to create a worktree and work inside it, naming the actual commands in order: create with the base commit as an argument of `git worktree add`, admit the placement with `speckiwi orchestrate preflight --role lane --lane-id --lane-plan`, do the code work there, harvest the deferred-mutation queue, replay it at the host root with `speckiwi orchestrate replay apply`, and release the workspace only after the harvest. Each section SHALL state the target under which it applies, so it does not contradict a phase-1 statement that the skill creates no lane workspace. Neither section SHALL restate the shared contract's reasoning; it SHALL point at `_shared/kiwi/worktree-lane.md` for the why and carry only the ordered steps.

#### Rationale

Declaring the contract in §0 gave the skills a pointer and no procedure: an agent reading either skill top to bottom finds nothing it can run, and the one section that mentions worktrees at all — wave-master §2.1 — refuses a delegation and hands the operator two manual recovery paths. A contract with no caller in the body is the documentation form of the kernel with no caller in `src/`, and this repository has now met that shape twice in one target. The steps must name real commands because the failure the shared contract was written to prevent was a command sequence that looked right and detached HEAD; prose that stops short of the command cannot be checked against the tool at all.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Each skill carries a numbered worktree section, in every shipped rendering.
- [x] AC-2: The section names `git worktree add` with the base commit as an argument on the same command, and does not instruct a separate checkout of that commit.
- [x] AC-3: The section names `orchestrate preflight` together with `--role lane`, so the placement is admitted by the gate rather than assumed.
- [x] AC-4: The section names `orchestrate replay apply` as the step that lands the lane's deferred mutations at the host root.
- [x] AC-5: The section states that release happens only after the harvest, and names both in that order.
- [x] AC-6: The section names the target under which the procedure applies, so it cannot be read as a claim about a phase that creates no lane workspace.
- [x] AC-7: The section points at the shared contract rather than restating its reasoning.

### FR-FLOW-124 — kiwi-pipeline runs the full cycle by default, with --none-cycle as the single opt-out

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.9.0-pipeline-cycle-default |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The kiwi-pipeline skill SHALL treat the §2.5 five-stage research-to-implementation chain as its default behaviour rather than an opt-in mode, and SHALL provide exactly one opt-out, spelled `--none-cycle`, that restores single-next-step recommendation from Table T1. The implicit `--run` that cycle entry carries today SHALL attach only when the invocation supplies a work input, enumerated as: inline work text, a research document path, a GitHub issue number, `--from=<stage>`, `--req-filter`, or `--plan-run-id`. `--run` SHALL NOT be a member of that enumeration — it asks for execution, not for a unit of work — and `--run` alone SHALL keep its prior meaning of spawning the single next Table T1 candidate behind the §6.1 gate. The implicit run SHALL NOT attach to an invocation whose entire content is status or inspection arguments, and `--target` alone SHALL NOT count as a work input because it names a scope rather than a job. When the invocation is ambiguous the skill SHALL resolve to no work input. `--cycle` SHALL remain accepted and SHALL be declared behaviourally inert in exactly one place.

#### Rationale

User-directed 2026-08-13: make --cycle the default and add --none-cycle. The work-input condition is not a dilution of that directive — FR-FLOW-026, already verified, splits on exactly this line ("Given a work input it SHALL run /kiwi-srs ... When invoked without a work input it SHALL advance the cycle from the last pipeline.jsonl event via Table T1") and never mentions a --cycle flag, so the flag was the divergence and the flip closes it. Without the condition, the skill's own trigger list ("파이프라인 상태", "pipeline status") turns a read-only status question into SRS mutation, plan files, code writes, and implemented-to-verified transitions. --cycle stays accepted because installed skill copies lag the repository by contract and kiwi-wave-master keeps emitting it; in agent-read natural language an unknown flag has no defined handling.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: §1.2 of every shipped rendering opens with one sentence stating that the default behaviour is the §2.5 full cycle and that `--none-cycle` is the opt-out, naming both the chain and the flag.
- [x] AC-2: §1.2 carries a `--none-cycle` row whose cells name the restored single-next-step recommendation behaviour.
- [x] AC-3: No rendering still carries the sentence keying the implicit run on cycle entry (`--cycle` 진입 (`--run` 미지정) → `--run` 암묵 활성); the implicit run is stated as conditional on a work input instead.
- [x] AC-4: A closed enumeration of what counts as a work input is stated, and it names `--target` alone as not a work input.
- [x] AC-5: An ambiguity tie-breaker is stated that resolves to no work input.
- [x] AC-6: `--cycle` is declared accepted and behaviourally inert in exactly one place per rendering, with the lagging-installed-copy reason given.

#### Research / Analysis

- Five-member decision committee, 2026-08-13, all read-only. Members 1 (contract integrity), 2 (blast radius) and 4 (API design) independently converged on binding the implicit run to a work input; member 5 (testability) established that "flip the default and leave the implication sentence as-is" is not a design but a non-choice, and supplied the assertion that refuses it. ### FR-FLOW-125 — Contradictory kiwi-pipeline option combinations are refused at entry, and the opt-out is reachable in natural language

| Field | Value |

| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The kiwi-pipeline skill SHALL refuse at entry, rather than resolve by precedence, any invocation combining `--none-cycle` with an argument that presupposes the cycle: `--cycle`, `--from=<stage>`, or `--wt`. `--stats` SHALL be declared to imply `--none-cycle`, so that the concept "do not run the chain" has one owner and one derived spelling rather than two unrelated-looking names. The skill SHALL declare `--no-cycle` an unrecognised spelling and SHALL refuse it by name rather than ignore it. §1.2 SHALL carry natural-language rows mapping status phrasings to the opt-out, and the skill description SHALL state the new default and the opt-out.

#### Rationale

The two branches differ by an entire five-stage chain that mutates the repository, so silent precedence hides the split until code has already been written. `--stats` is the subtler defect: today it is coherent only because everything is off by default, and after the flip its "실행 없음" clause either secretly suppresses the chain (a duplicate entry point) or contradicts itself. The misspelling matters because every other opt-out in the suite is `--no-*` — a reviewer's fingers will type `--no-cycle`, and an opt-out that is silently ignored runs the whole chain. The natural-language rows matter because §1.2 is a trigger-phrase map and the description is the routing surface on which "파이프라인 상태" arrives; ship the flag without them and a Korean-speaking user has no way to reach the opt-out.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The refusal list names `--none-cycle` paired with each of `--cycle`, `--from=`, and `--wt`, and states that the combination is refused at entry rather than resolved by precedence.
- [x] AC-2: `--stats` is stated to imply `--none-cycle`, in exactly one place, with the run-or-not versus what-to-print axis distinguished.
- [x] AC-3: `--no-cycle` is named as an unrecognised spelling that is refused by name, and no rendering uses `--no-cycle` as a real flag.
- [x] AC-4: §1.2 carries natural-language rows mapping status phrasings (상태, status, 다음 단계 추천, next step) to `--none-cycle`.
- [x] AC-5: The skill description states both the new default and the `--none-cycle` opt-out.

Covers the entry refusal naming --none-cycle with each of --cycle, --from= and --wt with precedence resolution explicitly excluded and no hedge; the --stats implication stated exactly once with both axes named; --no-cycle refused by name and absent as a real flag row; the status-phrasing trigger cell; and the description. --stats --wt was added to the refusal after review found the pair undefined — --stats implies --none-cycle, which is refused with --wt. |

### FR-FLOW-126 — The work-mode routing exclusion is keyed on delegated wave entry, not on the cycle being active

| Field | Value |

| Type | functional |

| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |

| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The kiwi-pipeline §2.8 work-mode routing exclusion SHALL be keyed on delegated entry — `--from=<stage>` skip-authoring entry, a parent wave or orchestrator spawn context, or the caller's explicit body-scope declaration — and SHALL NOT be keyed on the cycle being active. §2.8 SHALL additionally state that running the default cycle alone does not exclude an invocation from the router, and that a direct user invocation with no parent and no `--from=` remains subject to §2.8. The two recorded reasons for the exclusion SHALL survive on the restated line.

#### Rationale

Both recorded reasons are properties of a delegated wave run, not of a flag: kiwi-tdd's three always-HALT gates defeat the unattended completion a wave cycle requires, and kiwi-tdd emits no plan, worklog or review artifacts, so the wave-close evidence bundle cannot be assembled. Neither holds for a solo user typing a step-sized request. Keyed on the cycle being active, the exclusion swallows its own trigger once the cycle is the default: §2.8 becomes dead for every invocation, and FR-FLOW-039 and FR-FLOW-117 — both verified — become unreachable prose. The explicit "default cycle alone does not exclude" clause is required because a reader who knows the cycle is the default would otherwise re-derive the dead gate; it also makes the semantically-identical restatement "기본 사이클 진입은 적용 대상이 아니다" self-contradictory and therefore unwritable.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: No rendering still carries the literal sentence keying the exclusion on the cycle flag (`--cycle` / `--from=` 진입은 본 라우팅의 적용 대상이 아니다).
- [x] AC-2: The surviving exclusion names delegated entry — `--from=`, a parent wave/orchestrator spawn context, or a body-scope declaration — and is stated without hedging.
- [x] AC-3: §2.8 carries a clause stating that running the default cycle alone does not exclude an invocation from the router.
- [x] AC-4: §2.8 states that a direct user invocation with no parent and no `--from=` remains subject to the router.
- [x] AC-5: The two recorded reasons — kiwi-tdd's always-HALT gates defeating unattended completion, and the missing plan/worklog/review artifacts for the evidence bundle — survive on the restated line.
- [x] AC-6: The FR-FLOW-039 evidence is strengthened from whole-body token presence to an assertion that goes red when the gate becomes unreachable.

Mutation-proved: reverting the key to --cycle goes red, and so does deleting the default-cycle-alone clause. The first draft keyed on a disjunction that included --from=, which the pre-flip sentence also carried and which was therefore green on the text this requirement exists to remove; independent review caught it and the key is now the word for delegation itself. |

### FR-FLOW-127 — Every kiwi-pipeline gate keyed on the cycle flag is re-keyed on the condition it was written for

| Field | Value |

| Target | 2.9.0-pipeline-cycle-default |

| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

Every kiwi-pipeline gate and carve-out currently keyed on the `--cycle` token SHALL be re-keyed on the condition it was written for. The `multi-candidate-ambiguous` gate SHALL decide by candidate count — standing down when the next step is uniquely determined and firing when two or more candidates exist, inside the §2.5 chain or outside it — stated in the §0.AG row itself rather than in prose below the table, with the gate_id string unchanged. The `pipeline-start-candidate-ambiguous` row SHALL carry its own scoping the same way. The refusal that keeps `kiwi-commit-auto-push` out of the automatic chain SHALL be re-keyed off "단일 다음-단계 추천", SHALL remain unhedged, and SHALL NOT claim the hop requires an explicit user selection, which §6.1 contradicts. The `self-recursive-spawn` guard SHALL fire when two own-skill events have no child event between them, and every site that specifies it — the §0.AG row, §0.5, §6.5, the Table T1 self row and §10 — SHALL specify that same test and the same action. No statement anywhere in the body SHALL remain conditioned on the `--cycle` token except the single inert declaration, its §1.2 matrix row, the contradictory-combination refusal, and the `--no-cycle` guard.

#### Rationale

Each of these is a user-confirmation or irreversibility brake whose trigger the flip makes constant. The multi-candidate exemption's own premise — the chain is fixed so there is no choice — is false for Table T1 advancement, whose feasibility row forks to kiwi-planner or kiwi-srs-research; keyed on the flag, the gate retires repo-wide. The commit refusal is the one that matters most: the row it excludes is kiwi-review-fix-loop to kiwi-commit-auto-push, and it is excluded by being scoped to single-next-step recommendation, which the flip reduces to a residual mode — leave it and the default cycle can push. The self-recursion guard trips only when the immediately preceding events are kiwi-pipeline, but four Table T1 rows route back to kiwi-pipeline and a default cycle interleaves five child events between re-entries, so the guard can no longer fire while each re-entry now costs a full chain instead of one printed suggestion.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The §0.AG `multi-candidate-ambiguous` row decides by candidate count — it stands down when the next step is uniquely determined and fires when two or more candidates exist, inside the §2.5 chain or outside it — and the rule is stated in the row cells, not in prose below the table.
- [x] AC-2: The gate_id string `multi-candidate-ambiguous` is unchanged.
- [x] AC-3: The refusal keeping `kiwi-commit-auto-push` out of the chain no longer keys on single-next-step recommendation, is stated without hedging, and does not overclaim that the hop requires an explicit user selection, which §6.1 contradicts.
- [x] AC-4: Every site that specifies the self-recursion test — the §0.AG row, §0.5, §6.5, the Table T1 self row, and §10 — specifies the same one: the gate fires when the previous own-skill event's `next_hint` is `kiwi-pipeline` AND this invocation followed it automatically, and a user re-invocation is explicitly excluded so that a cycle followed by a status check followed by a cycle does not error.
- [x] AC-5: No statement anywhere in the body remains conditioned on the `--cycle` token except the single inert declaration, its §1.2 matrix row, the contradictory-combination refusal, and the `--no-cycle` guard.
- [x] AC-6: The `pipeline-start-candidate-ambiguous` row carries its own scoping in the row cells rather than only in §3's prose.
- [x] AC-7: No rule below §0.2 — §0.9's spawn-mode row, §12's degradation note, or the §1.2 work-input-less bullets — still describes spawning as gated on a flag the default does not supply.

#### Requirement

No shipped kiwi-pipeline rendering SHALL carry a claim about its own effects that the default flip makes false. The §0.2 declaration that the skill mutates nothing by default SHALL be restated to name what the default now reaches: the SRS through kiwi-srs, the working tree through kiwi-pm and kiwi-coder, and requirement status through kiwi-review-fix-loop --close-reqs; the §2.6 worktree exception SHALL survive that restatement. The `--auto`-alone option-matrix row SHALL be restated so it is not conditioned on `--cycle` 미지정. The §11 invocation table SHALL describe the new default for a bare invocation, and the §8.2 emit shape SHALL cover a run that executed a chain rather than only a recommendation. The behaviour of `--wt` without other arguments SHALL be stated.

#### Rationale

§0.2 is the 25th line of the document and the first safety statement a reader meets; leaving it puts a false claim where it will be trusted. The `--auto` row is the largest blast radius in the whole change and has zero test coverage: as written it says --auto alone recommends without executing, conditioned on a clause the flip makes never true, so --auto silently becomes an unattended full-chain run whose inter-stage gates the decision committee resolves. §11 sits roughly four hundred lines from the edit and is the section a partial landing forgets. `--wt` alone is harmless today because there is no cycle to isolate, and engaging under the new default it creates a worktree and, under --auto, opens a PR. FR-FLOW-027 AC-4 requires every rendering to state the §2.6 exception, so the restatement must keep it rather than replace it.

- [x] AC-3: The `--auto`-alone row is not conditioned on `--cycle` 미지정 and states what `--auto` alone does under the new default.
- [x] AC-4: §11's bare-invocation row names the cycle and states that it spawns rather than advises, and no §11 row routes a status phrasing to an immediate spawn.
- [x] AC-5: §8.2's emit shape covers a run that executed the chain — the summary and notes fields name the hop reached and the gate that halted it — and the paragraph saying so appears exactly once per rendering.
- [x] AC-6: The behaviour of `--wt` supplied without other arguments is stated in §1.2, and §2.6 carries the same work-input condition rather than creating a worktree unconditionally.
- [x] AC-7: No claim above §0.2 — the body's one-line self-description, the responsibility list, or §0.1's scope line — still describes an advisory-only skill.

#### Requirement

The refusal's object is a flag, so once the flag is not what starts the chain, a literal reading permits a bare `/kiwi-pipeline` — which is exactly the fixed five-stage chain the sentence exists to forbid. #### Requirement

Every existing assertion that pins the pre-flip contract SHALL be rewritten into an assertion that drives the new one, and SHALL NOT be deleted. Each rewritten assertion SHALL be mutation-proved independently: the shipped Markdown is edited to the plausible wrong wording, the assertion is confirmed red, and the edit is reverted. Assertions SHALL be scoped to the section or table row under test rather than to the whole document, and SHALL iterate the four shipped kiwi-pipeline renderings including the .agents mirror, and the three kiwi-wave-master renderings, which the mirror excludes by design. Every requirement whose Acceptance Criteria or Verification Evidence the flip falsifies — FR-FLOW-026, FR-FLOW-039, FR-FLOW-052, FR-FLOW-100 and FR-FLOW-117 — SHALL be amended with its own change note rather than left asserting prose that no longer says what it claims.

#### Rationale

Three existing assertions do not merely go quiet under the flip, they mandate the defect and will go red against the correct fix: the multi-candidate gate row assertion requires the exemption to name the cycle flag, the followup-consistency assertion pins the dead exclusion sentence verbatim with the comment that it must be unchanged, and the orchestrator-routing assertion requires the refusal to name the flag. Deleting them is the recorded failure mode. Section scoping is required because the token --cycle appears in eight sections of the pipeline body, so a whole-document search is satisfied by sections unrelated to the one under test; the repo already carries one such assertion, a disjunction over a twenty-four-line section that stays green on --from= alone. Amending the five requirements is not bookkeeping: leaving them verified against prose that has moved is the same failure this project has already recorded, where a claim is asserted once and nothing re-reads it.

### FR-FLOW-131 — kiwi-orchestrator declares one terminal review-loop obligation binding all three rungs

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.10.0-terminal-review-loop |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The kiwi-orchestrator SHALL declare, above its rung subsections, one terminal review-loop obligation binding R-STEP, R-PLAN and R-ORCH: a boundary that records a pass MAY do so only when a `/kiwi-review-fix-loop` execution exists whose `--base`/`--head` window covers the commit range that boundary judges. The obligation SHALL be stated exactly once, SHALL name all three rungs, SHALL state that the hop runs exactly once per boundary, SHALL state that no rung is exempt, and SHALL carry no hedge. It SHALL NOT be phrased as unconditional execution: a child returning `NEEDS_USER` or `FAILED` halts the parent under §0.4, so the contract is that the hop is not keyed on the child's return value and the §0.4 halt is the only non-execution path. An empty commit window SHALL record `not-applicable-empty-window` and SHALL NOT fire the gate; a run that halted after commits landed SHALL record `skipped-run-halted`, SHALL NOT auto-run the hop, and SHALL NOT be reported complete. Each rung SHALL implement the hop it is bound to — a declared boundary with no invocation is the declared-gate-with-no-predicate failure this skill's own gate table forbids.

#### Rationale

User-directed 2026-08-13: both orchestrating skills must guarantee the feedback loop runs at the end. Today R-STEP has no review hop at all — kiwi-tdd's subtree contains no code review, so a promoted step ships on red/green plus regression alone. A rule phrased "at Phase 4" is unreachable on R-STEP and R-PLAN, which terminate in Phase 1.c'; a rule phrased "each wave" is unreachable on the two rungs that have no waves. Binding the rule to the boundary that writes a pass verdict is the one formulation all three rungs provably have, and it reuses the windows the skills already resolve. The empty-window branch is load-bearing: without it the gate fires on requirements-only and pre-landing-halt runs, which is the declared-gate-with-no-predicate failure the skill's own gate table forbids.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: §4.5's preamble, above its first rung subsection, carries a terminal-hop rule that names R-STEP, R-PLAN and R-ORCH, names `kiwi-review-fix-loop`, states the hop runs exactly once per boundary, states that no rung is exempt, and carries no hedge.
- [x] AC-2: The rule states that the hop is not keyed on the child's return value and that the §0.4 halt is the only non-execution path, naming `TASK_DONE`, `NEEDS_USER`, `FAILED` and §0.4.
- [x] AC-3: The rule states the empty-window branch as `not-applicable-empty-window` with the gate not firing, and the post-landing halt branch as `skipped-run-halted` with the run not reported complete.
- [x] AC-4: The obligation appears exactly once per rendering, in all four shipped copies including the .agents mirror.
- [x] AC-5: The R-ORCH rung discharges the obligation with an invocation of its own inside `§V.final-verify`, placed before the pass is recorded, windowed on `run_diff_window` and not carrying `--close-reqs`. A rung that only inherits the declaration is the declared-boundary-with-no-invocation failure the requirement forbids.
- [x] AC-6: `§V.final-verify` instructs writing the `terminal_review` record the run-close validator reads, names all four verdicts, states the window equality the validator refuses on, and requires the review's own fix to be committed before the close line is written. Without this instruction the validator's rule has no producer.

### FR-FLOW-132 — The R-STEP rung invokes the review loop before its close-out, and its flag paragraph stops being false

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.10.0-terminal-review-loop |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

§4.5.1 SHALL invoke `kiwi-review-fix-loop` in its own `Skill({...})` form over the step's commit window with `--base` and `--head` and `--no-pipeline-emit`, and SHALL NOT pass `--close-reqs`, because kiwi-tdd has already promoted the step requirement through promote_step_requirement and the loop skips any requirement that is not `implemented`, so `--close-reqs` would skip its entire denominator and still report TASK_DONE. The hop SHALL be placed before the validate / sync-index close-out and before the P.5 run lock release, since a review that edits code must run before the index close-out and while the lock still holds. The rung's post-return outcome count SHALL be restated to match the hop. The flag paragraph SHALL stop justifying non-propagation of `--max` and the pass-through options by the absence of their target gates on this path, because the review loop's own consent gates now exist on it, and the options that release those gates SHALL be propagated. The hop SHALL state that it does not modify tests authored in the red phase.

#### Rationale

kiwi-tdd's subtree contains no code review — grep for review vocabulary over its body returns nothing — so R-STEP is the widest of the three gaps, not the rung that deserves an exemption. An exemption cannot be stated safely either: any phrasing like "step-sized work is exempt" restates the size predicates the classifier already uses, so every future R-STEP route would self-exempt by construction. The flag paragraph is the one place the change cannot be made silently: it currently says the pass-through options target gates that do not exist on this path, and that becomes false the moment the hop exists, which under an unattended --auto run would stop the run at the child's consent gates with no flag able to release them. The test-inviolability clause is required because kiwi-tdd forbids weakening a red-phase test while the review loop's senior fixer carries no such constraint.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: §4.5.1 carries a `Skill({ skill: "kiwi-review-fix-loop" ... })` invocation form rather than a pointer to the §4.5 rule or an exemption sentence.
- [x] AC-2: The hop's arguments carry `--base`, `--head` and `--no-pipeline-emit`, and do not carry `--close-reqs`.
- [x] AC-3: The hop appears before the terminating emit, before the validate / sync-index close-out, and before the P.5 run lock release, verified by offset ordering rather than presence.
- [x] AC-4: The rung's stated post-return outcome count matches the number of outcomes the section actually lists.
- [x] AC-5: The flag paragraph no longer justifies non-propagation by the absence of the targeted gates on this path, and names the options propagated to the review-loop child.
- [x] AC-6: The hop states that it does not modify tests authored in the red phase.

### FR-FLOW-133 — The R-PLAN hop carries an explicit window and drops its return-value condition

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.10.0-terminal-review-loop |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

The R-PLAN second hop SHALL carry an explicit `--base` and `--head` window in addition to `--close-reqs`, because the orchestrated units have already committed by the time the hop runs, so a hop with no scope resolves against a clean working tree and falls back to the last five commits behind a user-confirmation prompt — which under `--auto` is resolved by the decision committee rather than by a user. That fallback would satisfy the new terminal obligation with a review of unrelated commits, converting a real gap into a recorded pass. The hop SHALL NOT be keyed on the child returning `TASK_DONE`; the §0.4 halt already makes the other two return values unreachable, so the condition is dead text whose removal is semantically neutral. The sentence declaring the hop the orchestrator's own policy rather than an inherited obligation SHALL survive unchanged.

#### Rationale

This is the single companion fix without which the new gate is worse than no gate. The review loop resolves its scope from an explicit range, then the working tree, then a five-commit fallback gated by a question; orchestrated units commit through kiwi-pm, so the tree is clean at the hop and the fallback is the live path. A gate satisfied by a false-clean execution records a pass over commits nobody chose to review. Dropping the TASK_DONE condition is separately safe: kiwi-pm is a closed three-state protocol and both non-TASK_DONE values already halt the parent through §0.4 and through the child-pipeline-needs-user-or-failed gate, so the condition restates a precondition that is unreachable-otherwise.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The R-PLAN hop's argument string carries `--base` and `--head` alongside `--close-reqs`.
- [x] AC-2: The rung states why the window is explicit — that a scopeless hop after committed units falls back to a five-commit range behind a prompt the committee answers under `--auto`.
- [x] AC-3: No line introducing the hop keys it on `TASK_DONE`, `완주` or `성공`.
- [x] AC-4: The replacement states what governs instead, naming `TASK_DONE`, `NEEDS_USER`, `FAILED` and §0.4. The "only non-execution path" formulation belongs to §4.5's preamble, which owns the obligation for all three rungs; restating it here would duplicate a rule with one owner.
- [x] AC-5: The sentence declaring the hop the orchestrator's own policy and not an inherited obligation survives, together with its `--close-reqs` / `verified` ground.
- [x] AC-6: The R-PLAN close-out records `outcome: "delegated-complete"` on its `dispatch-route` result line. The run-close validator recognises a delegating rung's close by that token alone, so without it this rung's boundary is invisible to the gate and the obligation is enforced on two rungs while reading as three.

### FR-FLOW-134 — kiwi-wave-master owns a run-scope terminal review hop instead of inheriting one

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.10.0-terminal-review-loop |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

kiwi-wave-master SHALL invoke `kiwi-review-fix-loop` itself over the run-scope window, immediately before its whole-run final verification so the hop's report lands inside that pass's evidence, using `--base` and `--head` resolved from `run_diff_window` and NOT `--close-reqs`. The section SHALL reject by name the reading that the pipeline chain's terminal hop is enough, and SHALL argue it from the unit of judgement rather than from disjoint denominators: the run window CONTAINS every wave window, so the two denominators necessarily overlap, and what makes the run-scope hop non-redundant is that a per-wave review sees only inside one wave and therefore never judges the interactions that cross wave boundaries — the `integration_items` the final verification already names for the same reason. The per-wave loop's presence SHALL become a precondition of recording a wave `complete` rather than only a finding raised afterwards, and the existing rule that a missing review-loop event in a wave's evidence window is raised as a verifier finding SHALL be preserved. The skill SHALL declare a gate covering a directly-invoked review loop returning `NEEDS_USER` or `FAILED`, because the existing child gate names only the pipeline and the halt would otherwise fall through to a committee-decidable class.

#### Rationale

Today the skill never calls the loop; it gets it as the last hop of the per-wave pipeline, so a wave whose pipeline halts earlier surfaces only as an after-the-fact finding. The run scope has no owner at all: the whole-run final verification exists precisely because per-wave verification sees only each wave's scope and an item in no wave's scope is never checked, and that argument transfers verbatim to review — cross-wave defects that no single wave window contains are structurally unreviewed. The gate matters most in the unattended path the directive is aimed at: with the halt falling to a committee-decidable class, an unattended run would auto-approve skipping the very loop this work exists to guarantee.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The skill carries a `Skill({ skill: "kiwi-review-fix-loop" ... })` invocation of its own, placed before the whole-run final verification section.
- [x] AC-2: The hop's window is resolved from `run_diff_window`, not from the last wave's window, and the hop does not carry `--close-reqs`.
- [x] AC-3: The section rejects by name the claim that the pipeline's terminal hop makes an owned hop unnecessary.
- [x] AC-4: The non-redundancy argument does not claim the two denominators are disjoint. It states the containment — the run window is a superset of every wave window — and rests the argument on the unit of judgement, naming the cross-wave interactions no per-wave review can see. A reader who checks a false disjointness claim finds the hop unjustified and deletes it.
- [x] AC-5: Recording a wave `complete` is stated to require the per-wave review loop's presence, not merely to raise its absence afterwards.
- [x] AC-6: The rule that a missing review-loop event in a wave's evidence window is raised as a verifier finding survives.
- [x] AC-7: The critical gate table declares a gate covering a directly-invoked `kiwi-review-fix-loop` returning `NEEDS_USER` or `FAILED`.
- [x] AC-8: The `--auto` safety gate enumerates the directly-spawned review child alongside the two children the skill already spawned, so its `NEEDS_USER` does not fall to a committee-decidable class.
- [x] AC-9: The wave-append re-entry re-runs the run-scope hop and the final pass in order, because the appended wave's commits are the only ones a run-scope review could newly reach and skipping the hop advances `run_diff_window.head_sha` past the window the close record already claims.

### FR-FLOW-135 — The terminal obligation is refused by name rather than opted out of, and its stale neighbours move with it

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 2.10.0-terminal-review-loop |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | - |

#### Requirement

Neither skill SHALL add an opt-out flag for the terminal review loop; applicability is derived from the commit window, so a run that wrote no code is covered by the empty-window branch rather than by an option. The spellings `--no-review-loop` and `--skip-review-loop` SHALL be refused by name through the existing unsafe-option refusal rather than silently ignored. Every statement the new hops falsify SHALL move with them: the orchestrator's phase-flow diagram row for the step rung, the shared loop-option contract's statement of which child the step rung routes to, and the stated post-return outcome count. The shared pipeline-event routing table's row mapping the step skill's completion to the review loop — which has been asserted since it was written but described a hop that never happened, because the step child emits no pipeline event and the rung writes a null next hint — SHALL be reconciled with what the rung now does.

#### Rationale

An opt-out flag would be a second spelling of a refusal both skills already own, and the suite has the precedent for the alternative: kiwi-pipeline refuses --no-cycle by name rather than ignoring it, on the stated ground that an ignored opt-out runs the whole chain. The stale neighbours matter because they are exactly the sites with no test readers — the phase-flow diagram is inside a fence so both the mutation ledger and the prose gate skip it, and the outcome count is unguarded prose. The routing-table row is the most interesting of them: the contract has asserted the hop this directive asks for since FR-FLOW-116, with no caller, which is the same shape as a kernel predicate nothing invokes.

- [x] AC-2: `--no-review-loop` and `--skip-review-loop` are named in the unsafe-option refusal and are refused rather than ignored.
- [x] AC-3: The orchestrator's phase-flow diagram row for the step rung shows the review hop.
- [x] AC-4: The shared loop-option contract's step-rung child set includes the review loop.
- [x] AC-5: The stated post-return outcome count for the step rung matches the outcomes listed.
- [x] AC-6: The shared pipeline-event routing table's step-skill row routes the step skill's completion at the review loop, and an assertion holds it there. The row already carried that value and so needed no correction — which is exactly why it had no reader, and why a later edit of the table could contradict the rung in silence.

#### Requirement

The release suite SHALL mechanically verify README.md's factual claims: every fenced `speckiwi` command line resolves to a registered CLI subcommand path, every internal anchor link resolves to an explicit `<a id>` anchor, every MCP tool name names a registered tool, and every load-bearing numeric count derives from the enumerable set it describes through an explicit phrase-to-enumerator registry. Illustrative examples opt out through a declared escape hatch rather than by weakening a check.

#### Rationale

-

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: README.md is inside the signature-parity net: a fenced speckiwi line naming a subcommand path absent from the live commander tree fails the suite, asserted by the negative case, not only by the green the real README already gives.
- [x] AC-2: Anchor links are checked against the explicit `<a id>` anchors the repository actually uses, not GitHub heading slugs — measured as an all-links false positive under slug rules — and a link to a missing id fails. The slug trap is asserted, not remembered: the heading-slug set and the link-target set must be disjoint.
- [x] AC-3: MCP tool names are checked against the runtime tool registry, which is the handler map minus its `resource:` entries; a token ending in * is a prefix-membership test over registered names, not an exact-name test, and the two family tokens are asserted present on the real README so that branch cannot ship covering nothing.
- [x] AC-4: The tool-name claim is scoped to Markdown table rows, which is the measured ground truth: scanning every backticked snake_case token instead admits status values and journal record types as false positives. This scope is part of the contract for the same reason the anchor convention is — an implementer who re-derives it will pick the wrong one.
- [x] AC-5: A numeric count adjacent to a registered noun phrase (tools, doctor checks, subcommands of a named namespace) is derived from its enumerable set, and a mismatch fails — the check that would have caught the recorded three-way 30/29/28 disagreement. The phrase registry is explicit; no free-form language inference. Every registered phrase must still match a line in the document, so a reworded sentence fails loudly instead of silently covering nothing.
- [x] AC-6: A `<!-- doc-lint: ignore -->` marker exempts the next fenced block or line, and non-shell illustration fences are skipped; an exemption is visible in the document rather than configured elsewhere, and the real README is asserted to carry none, so silencing a finding with a marker is visible in the diff.
