### FR-FLOW-158 — The validator's five names are held at zero across every shared file the orchestrator defers to, not only the one its §0.1 names

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | plan-3.0-04b, audit-28, follow-up-fr-flow-155 |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/04.orchestrate-gate-wiring.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

The five names by which a sentence can rule on the terminal line's validation - the MCP tool, `validateWavesJournal`, the gate it raises, `--engine`, and the common noun `검증기` - SHALL be measured at zero and asserted to stay zero across every file under `_shared/kiwi/` in every rendering that ships one, rather than in the single file `§0.1` of `kiwi-orchestrator` names. `_shared/kiwi/run-ledger.md` SHALL be in that corpus, because `§0.10` names it as the SSOT for the journal's write discipline and a contradiction planted there was measured invisible to every layer that reads this contract. Where a file legitimately uses one of the five names, the exemption SHALL be recorded for that file with the count that justifies it, rather than the name being dropped from the set for every file.

#### Rationale

`FR-FLOW-155` AC-8 drew its boundary at the one file `§0.1` defers to and wrote that boundary as the file the skill itself defers to. Measured: `§0` defers to ten shared files - `§0.1` waves-event.md, `§0.5` auto-option.md, `§0.6` loop-option.md, `§0.7` verify-loop.md, `§0.8` wave-decomposition.md, `§0.9` wave-srs-registration.md, `§0.10` run-ledger.md, `§0.11` workmode-policy.md, `§0.12` pipeline-event.md, `§0.14` worktree-lane.md - and nine of them are uncovered. A sentence in run-ledger.md using every one of the five names, saying the terminal line is not put through the validator and that a repeated diagnostic is answered by overwriting the line, left the three suites at 102 passing and 0 failing; verify-loop.md behaved identically. Authority is not the discriminator that separates the covered file from those two: `§0.10` names run-ledger.md as the SSOT of how a journal line is written, which is not a lesser claim on this procedure than owning the line's schema. The covered file is also porous within itself: it writes the bare noun `검증` 27 times legitimately, so only `검증기` could be banned, and a sentence built from `검증` alone saying the same thing was measured green inside it.
- [2026-08-29] Measured before this requirement was implemented. Its suite now sweeps all 49 files under _shared/kiwi/ in the four renderings, so the nine that were uncovered are covered and the 검증 path inside the covered file is closed on the sentence shape AC-5 records.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The corpus is every file under `_shared/kiwi/` in each rendering that ships one, enumerated by reading the directory rather than by a hand-written list, so a shared file added later is covered without an edit to this suite. Measured by adding a file to that directory carrying one of the five names and showing it red with no change to the test: a 3.8 KB probe carrying `--engine`, dropped into `skills/claude/_shared/kiwi/`, turned the sweep red while the other twenty-seven assertions in the suite stayed green. The per-rendering size assertion is a FLOOR rather than an exact count, because an exact count would turn red for a CLEAN file added as well, which is the property this criterion is buying. The bounds it runs under are written HERE rather than in the suite - `renderings 4`, `shared 12` per rendering and `corpus 49` in total - because a floor typed into a test cannot be defended by the check it bounds: measured, lowering the per-rendering floor to zero and narrowing the corpus to four files left every assertion green with 45 of the 49 gone, and the total is what reports the thirteenth file of `skills/etc` leaving. The corpus is that directory's MARKDOWN and the suite holds the directory's entry count equal to it, so a `.json` or `.yaml` shared contract landing there is red rather than silently unswept. A file in a SUBDIRECTORY is swept and accepted: the flat-directory path predicate was measured to turn a clean nested file red, which contradicts this criterion's own promise; measured now, the clean nested file is green and the same file carrying `--engine` is red. Measured before the change: the corpus was one file.
- [x] AC-2: `run-ledger.md` is in the corpus, and the sentence measured green there - the terminal line is not put through the validator, `orchestrate_validate` is optional, and a repeated `terminal-review-loop-missing` is answered by overwriting the line - is red in every rendering that ships the file. A sentence added to the same file carrying none of the five names stays green as the control, so the red is pinned on the names rather than on the file having been touched at all. Measured: red in all four renderings, planted one file at a time and each reverted to a matching md5, and `verify-loop.md` behaves identically. The control `종료 줄을 쓴 뒤에는 rung 을 lock 에서 읽고 재계산하지 않는다.` left all 28 assertions green in the same file. The plant fires the name sweep and NOT the AC-5 shape ban, so the red is attributable to the names alone. That attribution holds by four characters - the plant's anchor sits 64 characters from its first permission verb and the ban's radius is 60 - so the suite asserts the plant clears the shape ban rather than leaving the margin to prose; measured, the same plant under a radius of 80 fires both and that assertion is what reports it.
- [x] AC-3: Each of the five names is counted across the whole corpus before the assertion is added and the counts are recorded in this requirement. Measured over 49 files - 12 in `skills/claude`, 12 in `skills/codex`, 13 in `skills/etc`, which alone ships `local-llm-profile.md`, and 12 in `.agents/skills`: every one of the five is ZERO, under AC-4's widened patterns and its normalisation as well as under the narrow ones they replace. The set is held to `names 5` against this requirement's own text, so narrowing it is a requirement diff rather than a line in the suite. No file needs an exemption today and the table is empty. A file where a name is not zero does not cause that name to be dropped from the set: that file is given a named exemption carrying its count and its reason, so a later reader can tell an exemption from an omission. Because the table is empty, both directions of the resolver are asserted on it directly rather than left untried - an unexcused count fails, a row whose count no longer matches fails, and a row whose use has gone away fails as stale - and both were measured end to end: planting `--engine` in `wave-decomposition.md` with the row present went green, and removing the plant with the row still there went red as stale. The reason table is asserted the same way and for the same reason, on constructed rows in both directions: a row with no reason and a reason with no row are each reported, where a check written only over the empty table iterates zero times and compares nothing. Measured before the change: `검증기` was the only one of the five narrowed for this reason, and it was narrowed for every file rather than for the one file that needed it.
- [x] AC-4: `orchestrate-validate`, which passed `/orchestrate[_ ]validate/` in the front-half measurement, is red here. Each pattern's case sensitivity and separator set is decided here rather than inherited: the MCP tool is case-insensitive over `-`, `_` and space, so this tree's three spellings for one thing are one hit, while `orchestratevalidate` is NOT admitted because nothing writes it; the validator function likewise, with an optional separator between its three words; the gate likewise over the same three, requiring all four words, so the legitimate bare `terminal_review` is not a hit; the engine flag requires the leading `--`, because bare `engine` is the journal's own field, written 44 times here - 11 per rendering, 8 in `waves-event.md`, 3 in `run-ledger.md`; the common noun has no case or separator and josa attaches without a boundary, so a substring already reads `검증기가`. Four spellings that walked past these patterns in a shipped file are closed BEFORE they run, not by widening: the full-width `ｏｒｃｈｅｓｔｒａｔｅ＿ｖａｌｉｄａｔｅ`, the class `FR-FLOW-155` AC-3 records `ＭＣＰ` bypassing, folded by NFKC; the markdown-escaped `orchestrate\_validate`, unescaped; the name written with two spaces or a tab, collapsed - a step doing that work under no assertion until removing it went green; and a name folded at a separator across a soft line break, rejoined by reading one markdown BLOCK at a time, with each line of a CODE FENCE its own block because a renderer draws those apart too and joining them turned two fields of one JSON fence red. Block units do not by themselves keep a block short here: the longest measured 2,451 characters, a JSON fence read as one sentence, 1,137 once fences split - so what bounds the ban's reach is AC-5's radius. Measured after: the five names are still zero over 49 files; NFKC rewrites only `…`, 125 times, the escape rule only `\|` and `\"`. Not attempted: a different word for the same thing, the class `FR-FLOW-155` AC-4 records, which no name list closes.
- [x] AC-5: The `검증` path inside the covered file is decided. CHOSEN: the assertion, not the accepted cost. It is keyed on the sentence's shape - the terminal line named, within `radius 60` characters of one block, joined to a verb letting its validation be skipped or the line rewritten - over the whole corpus, not one file. `검증` is not in the pattern: the noun is avoidable and the shape is not. Measured on the sentence the Notes quote: green before, red now, carrying no name, and the 49 files hit it zero at radii 24-1000 in four block modes. The vocabulary is `verbs 49` SPELLINGS, not stems, ONE ENTRY PER SPELLING with the sentence only it catches: probed as a whole it survives losing one. Every entry names the LEMMA it is a form of, and its three slots - plain declarative, `-고`, `-ㄹ` - are BUILT from that stem and asserted filled over `lemmas 16`, 48 cells, none open. As prose it was false where it stood: 6 of 36 open, all six in the two slots it named. SPACING is decided on both sides of the ban: `종료줄` is the same anchor, and a space the list writes is optional in the verbs too, so `하지않는다` is `하지 않는다`. Measured: 18 of the 21 cells whose spelling carries a space passed written solid before, 0 after, the corpus still zero and nothing held green refused, though it widened AC-6's false-refusal class to the solid spellings; it also makes two spellings of one verb one lemma. Exemptions carry a reason and the standing spelling - the copula's `-다` for the rule's `-ㄴ다`, twice - and a row fails as stale, or if its removal opens no cell. Stems were refused: a stem reads a prohibition as the permission it negates; the Notes carry that. `통과한다` is outside the list, the causative `통과시킨다` inside it, both asserted. It SUBSUMES `FR-FLOW-155`'s rewrite verb list, asserted from that list's source. What it gives up: a CLOSED list anchored on `종료 줄`, so AC-6's five classes pass, each asserted green there by name; and replacing an entry with its sample passes too, only Hangul spelling held here.
- [x] AC-6: What this requirement does NOT guarantee. That an agent reads a shared file, or obeys it. It does not reach a file outside `_shared/kiwi/` - a skill body, a `docs/` page, a `kiwi-wave-master` rendering (`FR-FLOW-156`'s), as a path predicate. It does not catch a contradiction matching none of the five patterns after AC-4's normalisation and not taking AC-5's shape - `FR-FLOW-155` AC-4's class, narrower; widening the NAME list is not the repair (the Rationale's 27 legitimate `검증`), so AC-5 closes on the shape. Two spelling residuals are decided: a name folded MID-WORD rejoins `--eng ine`, which no separator set reaches, and the typographic-dash flag is absent. A sentence split across two LIST ITEMS, or two lines of a CODE FENCE, is read as two: a renderer draws a boundary at both; the Notes carry what joining refused. An unbalanced or nested fence turns joining off for the REST OF THE FILE, missing a permission after it, recorded not closed: the corpus cannot reach it (148 delimiters, all three backticks, even per file) and forcing balance trades a miss for a false one. AC-5's vocabulary is closed, not complete; FIVE classes pass it, each asserted green by name. Censused, 16 lemmas by 14 endings, 224 forms: the open are TWO of the five - another conjugation outside the three slots, over ten endings, and the polite register, 11, one per lemma not entered as a prefix, measured 0 in 1,507 plain endings. The other three are not conjugations and sit OUTSIDE it: a verb derived from a root it carries (`생략된다`), a synonym or the pronoun form (`필수가 아니다`; the pronoun open for want of an anchor), and a slot spelled with a space the list does not write (`생략 한다`). It errs the other way in a CLASS, not once: its boundary is LEFT-side only, so all 49 spellings are refused with a negation after them (`생략할 수 없다`), the fold widening it to the solid ones; measured absent, asserted red. It does not judge whether a shared file's content is correct, only whether it rules on this procedure.

| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/02.promotion-chain-wiring.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

The skill that performs the `implemented` to `verified` transition SHALL call `check_acceptance_criteria` between registering evidence and changing status, in every rendering it ships, and its tool allowance SHALL admit that call under the same `--close-reqs` self-mode restriction that already bounds the other two. The sentence that governs the call SHALL require, for each acceptance criterion it checks, a named test identifier that passed it — a file path and test name, or the `reference` the immediately preceding `add_verification_evidence` registered for that same criterion — and SHALL forbid checking a criterion for which no such identifier is named. The transition rule of `kiwi-coder`, which registers evidence but checks no criterion, SHALL name one target status across every rendering and that status SHALL be one the code gate admits. This closes the half of the gap where the promotion is impossible: `update-status.ts` refuses `verified` without every criterion checked, and no skill in the implementation chain could check one. It deliberately does not close the other half — the obligation it adds is prose, so an agent naming a test that does not exist is not refused at the check itself. A path-shaped fabrication is still refused one call later, because FR-NODE-174 resolves each path-like reference in the checkout; what survives is a reference the resolver never reads, written identically into both calls, and `FR-NODE-200` owns making the check demand evidence that covers the criterion it is asked to tick.

#### Rationale

The audit (docs/research/28, §3.3) found that the eight skills of the implementation and review chain call `check_acceptance_criteria` zero times — measured again at the time of writing, still zero in all of `kiwi-coder`, `kiwi-pm`, `kiwi-review-fix-loop`, `kiwi-planner`, `kiwi-tdd`, `kiwi-orchestrator`, `kiwi-wave-master`, `kiwi-hot-fix`, across three renderings and the mirror.
- [2026-08-28] Three skills call it, and they are not all requirement-authoring ones: `kiwi-srs` and `kiwi-srs-from-code` author requirements, while `kiwi-commit-auto-push` evaluates the match at commit time. `kiwi-review-fix-loop` narrows the gap further: its allowance names exactly `update_status` and `add_verification_evidence`, so under `--close-reqs` it has no means to check a criterion at all.
- [2026-08-28] That does not deny every promotion it attempts. `update-status.ts` refuses `verified` where a criterion is unchecked, so a requirement whose criteria were already ticked elsewhere clears that clause without the skill ever calling the check, and one carrying no criterion at all is refused by a neighbouring clause rather than by the unchecked one — the gate requires at least one.
- [2026-08-28] The correct order is already written down in this repository, in a skill that performs no promotion: `kiwi-srs-from-code` states evidence, then check, then transition. What makes this dangerous rather than merely broken is the direction of the repair: today a machine gate refuses the promotion outright, and this requirement replaces that refusal with a checkbox an agent ticks. Without an obligation binding each tick to a named test, the item trades a loud failure for a quiet falsehood.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: In every rendering that performs the promotion — the three under `skills/` and the mirror — the body names `check_acceptance_criteria`, and inside the section carrying the promotion sequence the first occurrence of that name sits between the first occurrence of `add_verification_evidence` and the first occurrence of `update_status`. The comparison is on character offsets within the enclosing section rather than over the whole file, because both other tool names appear elsewhere in these bodies and a document-wide comparison would be satisfied by unrelated mentions. It keys on the FIRST occurrence of each, so prose naming a tool ahead of the sequence would turn it red without the rule being broken — a false failure rather than a false pass. Swapping any two of the three turns it red, and so does removing the middle one. The three are named as tools rather than described in prose, so one vocabulary states the contract in every rendering; measured before the change, three renderings wrote step one as the English sentence `Add verification evidence` and were invisible to a scan keyed on the tool.
- [x] AC-2: The sentence governing that call requires a named test identifier per criterion and forbids checking one without it, and the whole section carrying that sequence is compared byte-exact against a checked-in golden — its heading to the next heading of any depth — so an inversion that preserves every token is refused as well as a deletion. Presence of the word alone is not accepted as evidence of the rule, because a presence check is satisfied by its own inversion; that is the lesson FR-FLOW-152/153 and FR-FLOW-155 AC-3 both recorded. The set of sections compared is DERIVED rather than listed: a promotion sequence is any numbered list inside `kiwi-review-fix-loop` naming `update_status` and `verified`, and the golden records every one found together with its path. A second sequence planted elsewhere in the skill is therefore a section the golden does not carry and fails, and a deleted sequence is a section the golden carries and fails. Measured: seven such sections exist — one in claude, two each in codex, etc and the mirror, because those three split the skill across `SKILL.md` and `references/extended-workflow.md`.
- [x] AC-3: The tool allowance of `kiwi-review-fix-loop` admits `check_acceptance_criteria` in all four renderings and the admission carries the same two bounds the existing two carry — `--close-reqs` and self mode — asserted in the same row as the tool name, so an admission stated without them fails. That row is found by its STRUCTURE, a section-zero table row, rather than by a word meaning `allows`, because a lexical key is defeated by a synonym and this one must separate the allowance from an artefact list naming the same tools and the same flag. The default path is asserted to remain a mutation prohibition, but that half is a presence check and therefore holds against deletion and NOT against inversion — the section-zero rows live outside the golden's seven sections, so `Normal mode does not mutate SRS, except when --close-reqs is implied` would pass. What is held against inversion is the allowance row itself. Widening the allowance to the default path is caught only when the widening also drops one of the three tokens from that row; freezing the section-zero table instead would cover it and would also freeze rows other requirements own, which is the cost AC-2 declines. Where a rendering additionally lists the tools its call log carries, that list is asserted to name the check too; measured, only claude carries such a line, so that assertion is vacuous in the other three and is kept as a drift guard for the one that has it.
- [x] AC-4: The transition rule of `kiwi-coder` names one target status in all four renderings for the branch where every criterion holds green evidence, and that status is `implemented`. Measured before the change, the four renderings did NOT agree: claude and etc wrote `verified` while codex and the mirror wrote `implemented`. The value is derived from `REQUIREMENT_STATUSES` rather than restated, so a status renamed in code and not here fails; the four renderings are compared to each other rather than each to a literal, so a future divergence fails even if one side is still right; and every occurrence of the rule in a file is read rather than the first, so a second statement carrying a different value cannot hide behind the first. The body names both the successor and the reason, asserted as two separate clauses because deleting either alone must be red: the skill that does perform the transition is `kiwi-review-fix-loop --close-reqs`, and the reason this rule stops short is that `kiwi-coder` never calls `check_acceptance_criteria`. It DOES register verification evidence — its section-zero mutation allowance admits `add_verification_evidence` and its mutation sequence calls it — so the half of the gate it fails is the all-criteria-checked half alone.
- [x] AC-5: The wording this requirement introduces is counted in the shipped tree before the change and recorded, so a test that would have passed on the old text cannot be mistaken for one that holds the new rule. Measured: `check_acceptance_criteria` was 28 occurrences across `skills/` and `.agents/skills/` and NONE was in the eight chain skills — recorded with that distribution rather than as a bare zero, because the bare token was not zero and a record saying it was would be false. Of the phrases the obligation is made of, the prohibition clause and its English counterpart were zero; the Korean phrase meaning `for each acceptance criterion` was NOT zero and is recorded as such, which is why the obligation is held by the golden and by section-scoped patterns rather than by that token.
- [x] AC-6: This requirement states what it does NOT guarantee, and each residual is measured rather than reasoned. It does not guarantee that an agent calls the tool — the artifact is instruction, and no assertion here observes a run. On a fabricated identifier the residual is NARROWER than the obvious reading: `update-status.ts` gates `verified` on three conditions, not two — every criterion checked, at least one evidence row with a non-empty reference, and (FR-NODE-174) that each path-like reference RESOLVES inside the checkout. A file-path fabrication of the shape this requirement itself prescribes is therefore refused even when repeated identically into `add_verification_evidence`, because the resolver finds no such file. What survives is a reference the resolver never reads — a command-shaped one starting with a shell prompt or a runner name, or one carrying no path — written identically into both calls; that hole is FR-NODE-200's and needs a code change, because no condition compares which criterion a tick and an evidence row are each about. On coverage: the golden reads the seven promotion sections and nothing else, so a sentence retracting the obligation elsewhere in the same file is caught only when it takes the form of a numbered list, which the derivation surfaces as an eighth section, and is NOT caught as prose. Other criteria here do read outside those sections — AC-3's allowance row and AC-4's transition rule — but by presence, which survives its own inversion. `test/skills/orchestrator-mutation-ledger.json` was considered for the residual and rejected on measurement: its consumer reads `skills/{variant}/kiwi-orchestrator/SKILL.md` alone and asserts every row's `find` occurs there exactly once, so a row quoting this skill matches zero times and fails that suite; its variant list also has no mirror axis. Giving the ledger a file axis is outside this requirement's scope.
- [x] AC-7: `speckiwi skills mirror --check` reports zero divergence. Provenance is not claimed as a criterion: a hand-edited mirror matching byte for byte is indistinguishable from a regenerated one in the artifact, so `regenerated rather than hand-edited` is recorded as method in the Implementation Notes with the numstat that shows it.

### FR-FLOW-160 — Every kiwi skill a shipped body names as an owner exists in the tree that ships it

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | critical |
| Tags | plan-3.0-02, audit-28 |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/02.promotion-chain-wiring.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

A shipped skill body SHALL NOT name a `kiwi-*` skill as the owner of a responsibility, the destination of a delegation, or the caller of a tool unless a directory of that name exists in the rendering that ships the body. Where a responsibility genuinely has no owner today, the body SHALL say that it has none and name the path that discharges it instead, rather than naming a skill that does not exist. The check SHALL derive the set of existing skills by reading the rendering's own directory rather than from a list, so a skill removed from the tree turns the sentences that name it red instead of leaving them to point at nothing.

#### Rationale

`kiwi-pm` assigns `verified` promotion and Stability changes to `kiwi-reviewer`, and `kiwi-coder` names it as the future owner of post-implementation gap review. That skill exists in no rendering: `ls -d skills/*/kiwi-reviewer` returns three ENOENTs. Measured at the time of writing, the name appears 15 times under `skills/` and 5 more in the mirror. A name that does not resolve is worse than a blank, because an agent reading it looks for a skill to invoke, finds nothing, and has no instruction for what to do instead — the same failure shape as a guard believed to be present. This is the second face of the promotion gap FR-FLOW-159 closes: the owner named for the promotion does not exist, and the skills that could perform it were not calling the tool it needs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Every `kiwi-*` token appearing in a shipped skill body resolves to a directory in the rendering that ships that body. The set of existing skills is read from the filesystem per rendering rather than restated as a literal, so removing a skill directory turns every body naming it red. The mirror is checked against its own directory listing rather than against `skills/codex`, because the mirror carries an exclusion list and a name legitimately present in codex may be absent there.
- [x] AC-2: The scan is bounded by an exemption list that is itself checked, not merely consulted. Each exemption names one token and one reason, and every entry is asserted to still be needed — an exemption whose token no longer appears anywhere fails, so the list cannot silently outlive what it excused. This is the soundness half FR-FLOW-155's judgement recorded as missing when an exemption is checked only for survival.
- [x] AC-3: The sentences that named a skill which does not exist name a real owner instead, and say the responsibility has none only where none does. Of the seven sites, five now point at a skill that exists — `kiwi-review-fix-loop` for verified promotion and for implementation review, `kiwi-srs-feasibility` for Stability changes — and two say the responsibility has no owner: the `kiwi-prd` entry, because no skill declares PRD authoring, and the review of a research report, which the reader performs. Baseline for the three vanished names, measured before the change: `kiwi-reviewer` was 15 occurrences under `skills/` and 5 in the mirror, across `kiwi-pm` and `kiwi-coder`; `kiwi-prd` and `kiwi-srs-reviewer` were one occurrence per rendering each — `kiwi-prd` in `kiwi-pm`, `kiwi-srs-reviewer` in `kiwi-srs-research` — which is 3 under `skills/` and 1 in the mirror apiece. After the change all three appear zero times in every rendering and the mirror, and that zero is asserted rather than assumed from the edit.
- [x] AC-4: The replacement is held against inversion, not only against deletion, by asserting both halves of each pointer: the sentence in `kiwi-pm` naming the skill a responsibility went to, and a sentence in that named skill declaring it. A pointer whose target disowns the work is as red as a pointer to nothing. Three pairs are asserted, one per reassigned responsibility — verified promotion and implementation review at `kiwi-review-fix-loop`, Stability changes at `kiwi-srs-feasibility` — in every rendering, with the mirror's exclusion list honoured and each body flattened first, because the renderings wrap at different widths and a rule split across two lines is the same rule. EVERY occurrence of an anchor must reach its owner, not merely one of them: measured per rendering, `verified 승급` stands in two places in `kiwi-pm`, `구현 리뷰` in one and `Stability 변경` in three, and an assertion satisfied by any one of them passed even when another mention was rewritten to name `kiwi-planner` — a skill that exists but nowhere declares that responsibility — which left a false owner in the shipped body with nothing to report it. The gap between an anchor and its owner is bounded by length rather than by a line break, because the body is flattened before matching and excluding a newline is therefore a dead condition, which left the table pipe as the only live boundary: measured on the clean tree one anchor then spanned 2,496 characters of `kiwi-pm` to borrow an unrelated section's mention, so replacing the owner passed and deleting both pointer sentences passed too. The longest legitimate match is 94 characters, so the reach is 120 — every real pointer is admitted and a sentence reaching across a section to a mention it does not own is refused — and each unreached mention is quoted in the failure message, so a false pointer is named rather than only counted. `test/skills/orchestrator-mutation-ledger.json` is NOT used to pin this text: its consumer reads `skills/{variant}/kiwi-orchestrator/SKILL.md` alone and asserts that every row's `find` occurs in that one file exactly once, so a row quoting `kiwi-pm` or `kiwi-coder` matches zero times and breaks that suite; its variant list also has no mirror axis. What this does not hold: renaming an anchor phrase itself drives its occurrence count to zero, and the first assertion reads that as a responsibility named nowhere and fails — but an edit that changes the anchor and that assertion together passes, and nothing here reports it.
- [x] AC-5: The scan reads bodies rather than every file: measured, `kiwi-*` tokens also appear in test fixtures, plan documents and research notes, and this requirement does not govern those. What that gives up is recorded — a fictional skill name written into a plan or a research note is not caught here, and a body naming a skill that exists in a DIFFERENT rendering than its own is caught only because the listing is read per rendering. It reads only the hyphenated `kiwi-*` form as well, so a body that names an owner as a bare English word is invisible to it: one such sentence stood in `kiwi-pm`'s frontmatter, was fixed by hand with this change, and no assertion here would have caught it or will catch the next one.
- [x] AC-6: `speckiwi skills mirror --check` reports zero divergence.

### FR-FLOW-161 — The set a close run must account for comes from the tool, and a run that closed none of it does not report done

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | critical |
| Tags | plan-3.0-03, audit-28 |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/03.close-reqs-gate.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

The skill that closes requirements SHALL obtain the set it is accountable for from `list_requirements` rather than extract it itself, SHALL give every requirement in the scoped subset exactly one disposition — closed, or excluded with a stated reason — and SHALL treat a run whose dispositions do not account for the whole scoped set as invalid. A run in which at least one requirement was eligible and none was transitioned SHALL NOT report `TASK_DONE`. Requirements the skill deliberately does not close — those resting on prose as verification evidence, and those whose stability is `draft` or `deprecated` — SHALL be excluded from eligibility but SHALL remain in the scoped set carrying their exclusion reason, so the accounting sees them. The terminal status value SHALL come from the enum `_shared/kiwi/pipeline-event.md` already declares; no new value is introduced.

#### Rationale

The audit (docs/research/28, §3.2) found that terminal status is decided by two conditions — every immediate fix applied, and regression passing — and that promotion results enter neither. A run that found candidates and closed none of them ends `TASK_DONE`. Measured at the time of writing: `list_requirements` appears exactly once in this skill across all four renderings, in claude's §0.8 read carve-out, and nowhere in codex or etc; the zero-candidate row reads `skip and report` in every rendering; the claude status rule at `SKILL.md:642` names only fixes and regression, and codex and etc state the field as a bare value enumeration. What makes narrowing the terminal condition insufficient on its own is who builds the candidate set: the skill extracts it, so extracting less is a way past any gate keyed on it, and adding a reporting duty to the same actor only produces a second self-declaration. Moving the denominator outside the skill is what turns under-extraction into a count that does not add up.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Every rendering instructs the skill to obtain the denominator by calling `list_requirements` with the run's target and `status: "implemented"`, and to resolve that target from `get_active_target` rather than assume one. That vocabulary reaches the stage that acts on it: the transition loop's domain and its artifact are stated in the terms the denominator defines — the loop runs over `eligible` and the artifact is `closed_reqs.json.scoped` — because defining the sets in one clause while the next clause iterates a set the skill extracted for itself moves the words without moving the source. Measured: claude defined `scoped` and `eligible` in one clause while the mutation loop in the following clause ran over `high-confidence REQ` and named its artifact `candidates`, so the two vocabularies coexisted and the operative one was the skill's own. Target resolution is confirmed by the stopping rule — a run that cannot resolve the target reports that it could not build the denominator and halts — and not by the tool name's presence nor by its proximity: measured, claude's §0 read-allowance row carries `get_active_target`, `summarize_target` and `list_requirements` inside a single bracket, so deleting the target-resolution instruction wholesale left both a presence check and a 400-character proximity check satisfied by that one row, while no allowance row can stand in for the stopping sentence. The tool allowance is judged by set equality over the allowance clause alone, with the prohibition clause on the same line and the read-allowance statement that follows it cut away, because filtering for three fixed names and asserting the count is three is bounded above by three and so catches removal while admitting addition: measured, adding `add_requirement` to the allowance clause and writing `4종` beside it passed. Measured before the change: the tool name appeared once in the whole skill, in claude's read carve-out, and zero times in codex and etc. Both calls are reads, so no tool allowance changes — claude's §0.8 already places the three reads outside its mutation prohibition and the codex and etc equivalents prohibit mutation only.
- [x] AC-2: Every rendering states the accounting identity — transitioned plus excluded equals the scoped set — and states that a run failing it is invalid. The identity is what makes under-extraction visible: a candidate quietly dropped leaves the counts unequal rather than leaving the gate unfired.
- [x] AC-3: Every rendering's terminal-status rule takes the promotion result as a condition, and states that a run with at least one eligible requirement and zero transitions does not report `TASK_DONE`. Measured before the change, the claude rule named only fixes and regression, and codex and etc stated the field as a value list with no rule at all — so the two halves are asserted separately, because a rendering can carry the enum and no rule. Two lines are additionally held byte-exact against a checked-in golden: the line that states the terminal-status rule, and the line that states the disposition identity. Both are located by derivation from the rule they carry, not by a pinned line number. The golden holds those two lines and NOT the sections around them: claude's terminal-status section also carries the `--no-pipeline-emit` paragraph, which `FR-FLOW-114` owns, and `FR-FLOW-155` refused whole-section freezing for exactly this reason — its Implementation Notes record that refusal, and record that the closed vocabulary it took instead turned seven legitimate neighbouring edits red. The identity line is in the golden because presence alone was measured insufficient: an edit that quotes the rule and then cancels it — `... 는 참고 지표일 뿐이며 강제하지 않는다` placed before the clause and `라는 낡은 규칙은 폐기한다` appended after it, with the original clause left intact between them — left both presence assertions green. That is the cheapest edit that disarms the gate, and only a byte comparison refuses it. What is given up: a contradiction placed elsewhere in the same section is read by the pattern checks alone, and a pattern check does not survive its own inversion.
- [x] AC-4: The deliberate non-closures stay in the scoped set and out of eligibility, and every rendering says so. A requirement whose evidence is prose, and one whose stability is `draft` or `deprecated`, is excluded with a reason rather than dropped: dropping it from the scoped set would make the identity in AC-2 blind to exactly the requirements a person still has to act on. A run in which only such requirements remain does not fire the gate. The stability axis is asserted separately from the prose-evidence axis: every rendering is checked for `draft` and `deprecated` being stated together with `eligible`, because one assertion does not cover the two exclusion grounds this criterion names. Measured: erasing `draft` and `deprecated` from the skill entirely, down to zero occurrences, left every assertion green, because neither value appeared in any pattern — half of the grounds this criterion names by name sat outside verification while the criterion read as covered.
- [x] AC-5: The reporting duty enumerates the scoped set by requirement rather than summarising it, and a run whose scoped set is empty reports the denominator's size and why the intersection came out zero. Without the enumeration nobody can check the identity by hand, and an identity nobody can check makes obtaining the denominator externally pointless.
- [x] AC-6: The terminal status value used is one the shared event contract already declares, asserted against `_shared/kiwi/pipeline-event.md` rather than against a literal, so a value renamed in the contract and not here fails.
- [x] AC-7: Two sentences in `kiwi-orchestrator` are corrected in every rendering, not one, because after this change both are false. The first is the R-PLAN rung's statement that this skill does not gate on what it skips. The second is the R-STEP rung's statement that a run skips its whole denominator and returns `TASK_DONE` regardless: once this requirement makes `denominator` a defined set, that sentence describes a retired mechanism in the new vocabulary, because a requirement already promoted is never in the denominator at all — there is nothing to count rather than something skipped. The orchestrator's own compensating gate is NOT removed; the double defence stays and only the description changes. Its survival is observed through the gate's own id, `plan-coverage-unclosed`, and not through the word `close-reqs`: measured, that word stands at eight places in the skill and one of them is a skill-invocation argument, so deleting the gate together with its three disjuncts still passed a check that looked for that word.
- [x] AC-8: This requirement states what it does not guarantee. It does not observe a run: every assertion reads instruction text, so a skill that carries the rule and ignores it is not caught here. It depends on FR-FLOW-159 having landed — without a means to check acceptance criteria every transition returns `MUTATION_DENIED`, and this gate would then fire correctly on runs nobody can pass. And it depends on FR-NODE-198: a requirement written with a status outside the enum never enters `list_requirements { status: "implemented" }`, so the denominator does not know it and the identity holds while the requirement is invisible. That one case is not covered by moving the denominator out, and AC-5's duty to report the denominator's size is what makes it visible instead. One further residual: the assertions reach their subjects through three anchor phrases belonging to this requirement — the accounting identity, the terminal judgement, and the exclusion, and not the `verified 승급` family, which belongs elsewhere — and an edit that renames an anchor while editing the assertion searching for it in the same change is not caught.
- [x] AC-9: `speckiwi skills mirror --check` reports zero divergence. This is a mechanical check run by hand at the release gate and NOT an automated assertion of this requirement's suite: no test runs that command against this repository's tree, and the existing mirror tests run against a temporary fixture root instead. A divergence introduced here is therefore caught at the release gate and not by this suite.

### FR-FLOW-162 — Three claims the skills make about the code are checked against the code, from one table

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | critical |
| Tags | plan-3.0-06, audit-28 |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/06.skill-code-contract-test.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

The suite SHALL hold three contracts between the shipped code and the shipped skill text, managed as rows of one table in which each row names (a) the code-side fact, obtained by importing the shipped module rather than by restating its value, (b) the rule that extracts the skill-side claim from disk, and (c) the comparison between them. The three contracts are: the argument names a skill attributes to an MCP tool; the claim that the deferred-mutation replay queue has no applying consumer; and the terminal-review verdict vocabulary together with which of its values discharge completion. No value SHALL be restated inside the test file, because a restated value is a third copy of the contract and reproduces the defect the table exists to catch. The code-side assertions SHALL sit in their own it blocks, separate from the skill-side comparisons, so that a mutation of a code constant reddens at the constant rather than inside a text comparison. Where the shipped skill text disagrees with the code, the text SHALL be corrected in all three renderings and the mirror regenerated from them.

#### Rationale

The audit (docs/research/28, section 5.1) found the same contract written twice, once as a TypeScript constant under src/ and once as prose under skills/, with almost nothing comparing the two: of the 59 files under test/skills/ only three read a constant out of src/core at all. A value changed on the code side therefore leaves the prose stating the old one and the suite green, and agents act on the prose. Four drifts were live at the time of writing. Item 01 took the status enum and item 02 took the cross-rendering mismatch, so three remain and this requirement takes them. They are not three instances of one shape: one is a name the code never had, one is a negative existence claim the code refutes, and one is a subset relation stated by position rather than by name. Holding them as rows of one table is what keeps the fourth from needing a fourth file.
- [2026-08-28] Correction: the 59-files-and-three measurement above is the plan document's (`docs/plan/3.0/06.skill-code-contract-test.md` §1-§2), not the audit's — `docs/research/28` never names `test/skills`. On the tree this landed on, `test/skills/` holds 70 files and five read a constant out of `src/core`; this suite is the sixth. And §5.1 lists five drifts: one, a Stability value passed into a Status argument, was repaired with item 01, leaving the four counted above.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Every argument name a skill states inside a call example of the form `tool { ... }` is a key of that tool's schema in `toolSchemas`, imported from `src/mcp/server.ts` at assertion time rather than listed. The extraction takes the balanced brace group following a tool name and reads only its top-level key positions, skipping quoted spans and nested groups: a `[^{}]*` body silently misses every example whose value contains a brace, which is how `reference: "{path:line}"` hid the only violation in the tree behind a scan that reported zero. Measured over the four renderings before the correction: 100 tools declaring 564 arguments, 153 markdown files, 136 call examples matched, 128 of them carrying at least one key, and exactly one unknown key, `add_trace_link.trace_intent`, at four sites. Those numbers live in three different places and only some of them survive the correction, which this criterion states rather than implying that one command shows them all: the census assertion holds the tool count, the file count and the 128 as floors and is reproduced with `NODE_ENV=test npx vitest run test/skills/skill-code-contract.fr-flow-162.test.ts -t census`; the 564 is held by the AC-5 code-side block; and the 136 matched examples and the unknown-key count were measured against the pre-correction tree, so neither is re-derivable from a tree the drift has left.
- [x] AC-2: The extraction rule's false-positive count over the current tree is zero, and the direction this criterion deliberately does not assert is named with its measurement. Requiring every call example to carry the tool's required arguments was measured to flag 28 sites in 5 shapes, nearly all of them legitimate abbreviation: a paragraph about relation encoding writes `add_trace_link { type: "Requirement", relation: "..." }` and means only those two. Asserting that direction would need an exception list, and an exception list is where the next defect hides, so the suite asserts only that a name the skill uses is a name the schema has. What is given up: an example omitting a required argument still reads as a complete call, and this suite does not say so. The one site this change rewrote was also missing `relation`, and it was supplied there by hand rather than by a rule.
- [x] AC-3: The claim that the deferred-mutation replay queue has no applying consumer is refused while the consumer ships. The code side is asserted by real import, not by a symbol-name string: `applyReplayPlan` is imported from `src/core/orchestrator/replay-apply.ts`, so renaming it fails the type check before any assertion runs, and `ORCHESTRATE_TOOL_BINDINGS` is searched for the binding whose path is `["replay", "apply"]`, whose argv is then produced by running `orchestrateArgv` rather than read off the record. The skill side has two halves. No line naming an orchestrate replay verb or the `--defer-srs-mutation` flag may carry absence vocabulary about that consumer; measured, that rule matched 4 lines before the correction and 0 after, with 0 false positives once the subject was narrowed from the bare word `replay`, which had picked up the verb-enum paragraph naming `replay-deferred-mutations`. And every section that names the plan verb must name the apply verb, both spellings derived from the binding; measured, 8 sections named the plan verb and 0 of them named the apply verb before the correction. The negative half is a vocabulary list and is stated as such in AC-8; the positive half is what bounds it, because a paraphrase that evades the vocabulary still leaves the section owing the apply verb. A derived verb that comes out empty is itself reported as a violation: measured, deleting the binding left the spelling as the empty string and `includes("")` passed every section, so the row went vacuously clean while only the code-side block caught the deletion.
- [x] AC-4: The terminal-review verdict vocabulary is imported from `TERMINAL_REVIEW_VERDICTS` and its discharging subset is compared against behaviour rather than against a constant. The discharging set is obtained by running `validateWavesJournal` over a completing run-close for each member of the vocabulary and collecting the verdicts that do not produce `terminal-review-loop-missing`; a source scan of `TERMINAL_REVIEW_DISCHARGING_VERDICTS` would stay green against a validator wired to a different list, and this repository has recorded that failure. The vocabulary itself is the single source of its own value and has nothing in the code to be compared against, so it is imported rather than observed, and that half of the sentence is stated here rather than overclaimed. The skill sites are derived from disk as the lines naming at least three of the four verdicts, so a line that drops one is still judged rather than leaving the corpus. Measured before the correction: 8 such lines, 2 per rendering, every one naming all four; thresholds of 3 and of 4 select the same 8, so the derivation is not sitting on a cliff. Each site must enumerate exactly the four verdicts, must state which of them discharge completion by name rather than by position, and must not place a discharging verdict on the non-discharging side. Before the correction every site said the last two do not discharge, which is false of `not-applicable-empty-window`, and the claude rendering of `kiwi-orchestrator/SKILL.md` said 766 lines earlier — `:1194` against `:428` — that an empty window does not fire the gate, the other renderings carrying the same contradiction at line numbers of their own.
- [x] AC-5: The code-side facts of all three contracts are asserted in `it` blocks of their own, holding no skill text, and what that separation can and cannot do is stated rather than assumed. Those blocks assert SHAPE and REACHABILITY: that `toolSchemas` is a populated live zod record, that both replay leaves are bound and the applying one encodes to an argv the CLI accepts, and that the observed discharging set is a non-empty proper subset of the vocabulary. They cannot assert VALUE, because a constant that is the single source of a value has nothing in the code to be compared against, and adding one here would be the second copy this requirement exists to abolish. The value mutations therefore redden in the skill-side rows, where the skill states the same thing independently. Measured: deleting `relation` reddens both blocks, deleting the replay binding reddens both, and removing a value from the discharging set reddens only the skill-side row, because a set of one is still a non-empty proper subset. Keeping the two kinds in separate `it` blocks is what lets a failing run say which side moved; merging them breaks this criterion.
- [x] AC-6: Each contract carries a floor on how many sites its extraction found, because an extraction that stopped matching reports zero violations and is indistinguishable from a clean tree. The floors are per bucket, are measured, and the set of buckets found must equal the set of buckets carrying a floor, so a rendering swept without a floor and a floor for a bucket that no longer exists both fail. A floor of zero is refused by an assertion rather than by convention. Measured floors: call examples 31 / 32 / 33 / 32 for claude / codex / etc / mirror; replay-subject lines 18 / 18 / 18 / 15 and plan-verb sections 2 each; verdict enumerations 2 each. Because the corpus is derived from disk, a file that vanishes leaves the corpus rather than throwing, and the floors plus the census are what report it: removing one shipped file was measured to produce 2 failed / 9 passed.
- [x] AC-7: The three drifts are corrected in `skills/claude`, `skills/codex` and `skills/etc` together, and `.agents/skills` is regenerated with `speckiwi skills mirror --write` rather than edited. `trace_intent` stops being stated as an argument of `add_trace_link` and becomes what it can actually be, a token inside `notes`, with the schema's seven argument names — `id`, `type`, `reference`, `relation`, `notes`, `dryRun` and `ignoreLock` — spelled out beside it so the sentence is itself checkable. Naming five of the seven and calling everything else silently dropped would be false of `dryRun` and `ignoreLock`, which reach `withSrsMutationLock` and perform a dry run and a lock bypass, and a correction that ships a fresh false statement about the schema is the defect this requirement exists to remove. The `--defer-srs-mutation` section stops saying the applying consumer is absent and names the shipped surface, while keeping the operative warning that a queue nobody harvests loses its mutations; and the verdict sentence names the discharging pair instead of pointing at a position. The three renderings share one section-numbering scheme — `§0.14`, `§0.G3`, `§6.2` and `§9.5` stand in all of them — and what differs is which FILE carries a section: `skills/claude` keeps §9 onward inline while `skills/codex` and `skills/etc` move it into `references/extended-workflow.md`. A correction is therefore transposed by section number but never by path or by line number. `_shared/kiwi/worktree-lane.md` is Korean in the claude rendering and English in the other two, so each was corrected in the language it already speaks. Two of the seventeen edited files under `skills/` ship CRLF, so every replacement was applied with the file's own line endings preserved and with its occurrence count asserted, a silent miss being the failure mode.
- [x] AC-8: This requirement states what it does not hold. The absence half of AC-3 is a vocabulary list, so a paraphrase that avoids every listed word passes it; only the positive half is a real bound. AC-4's site derivation loses a line that drops two of the four verdicts, and the per-rendering floor is what reports that loss, one line at a time. A site is a physical line, so a rendering that later rewraps an enumeration across two lines drops that site and fails its floor: a false red on a legitimate edit, taken deliberately over flattening first, which would let a rendering lose the rule and still be counted. Every skill-side assertion reads instruction text, so a skill that carries a corrected sentence and an agent that ignores it are not distinguished here. AC-9's probes pin each judge with one sample it must refuse and one it must pass, which catches a judge neutered into a tautology in either direction but not one that is subtly wrong where neither sample reaches; and AC-10's byte golden covers the verdict lines only, so a corrected sentence followed by one retracting it is still uncaught for `trace_intent` and for the replay sections. The census numbers are counts over the tree at the time of writing and are asserted as floors, so growth passes and shrinkage fails — with one exception named rather than hidden: the replay bucket's census floor is 12 against a measured 77, because the per-bucket floors below it already hold that corpus at 62 and the census there guards only against the sweep collapsing entirely. The fourth drift shape, a rule three renderings state with three different values, is not in this table: item 02 took it. The one consequence this requirement opened for the owner has since been closed — `FR-FLOW-121` AC-6 required the renderings to name the applier as still absent, which `orchestrate replay apply` refutes, and on 2026-08-28 it was corrected through a guarded status hop and now keys on the loss condition rather than on a component's presence.
- [x] AC-9: The suite refuses its own quiet disablement, because a checker that has stopped checking reports exactly what a clean tree reports. Three mutations of the test file were measured to survive before this criterion existed, and each is now closed by an assertion about the suite rather than about the skills. Deleting the `mcp-argument-names` row wholesale left every test green and only lowered the count from eleven to nine, so the table's row ids are asserted against the three contracts this requirement names. Rewriting that row's judge to compare a site against itself left even the count unchanged, so every row is handed one sample it must refuse and one it must pass, both assembled from that row's own code-side fact rather than typed out, and a judge neutered in either direction fails one of the two; a row that offers no probe fails as well. Freezing the per-rendering file lists into a literal of the day's 153 paths kept every floor and every census number intact, because a floor of 153 cannot tell a stopped sweep from a shrinking one, so the corpus paths are re-derived from disk and compared for exact equality. Measured after: deleting the row gives 1 failed / 13 passed, neutering the judge gives 1 failed / 16 passed, and the frozen list passes while the tree is unchanged and fails the moment one markdown file is added to a rendering — which is the first moment the freeze costs anything, and the control run with the derivation restored and the same file present is green.
- [x] AC-10: The shipped verdict lines are frozen in a byte golden at `test/skills/skill-code-contract.fr-flow-162.golden.md`, derived by the same rule AC-4 uses and keyed on the file rather than on the line number, so an edit above a rule does not rewrite the golden while a rendering that loses its verdict line loses a golden entry. This closes the cheapest edit that disables a rule while leaving every token in place: measured, appending a sentence retracting the discharge rule to an otherwise correct line kept all four verdicts present and both anchors in order, and the judge passed it, while an agent reads the retraction and acts on it. FR-FLOW-161 closed the same attack on its own rule line the same way, and this reaches the site nothing covered before — `_shared/kiwi/waves-event.md`, which lies outside the section golden `FR-FLOW-155` holds over `kiwi-orchestrator`. Measured: the retraction gives 1 failed / 16 passed at the `kiwi-orchestrator` site and 1 failed / 16 passed at the `waves-event.md` site. The golden is never written from the test, only offered as a `.actual` file to be read and copied, because a golden that refreshes itself on failure records whatever was done last.

### FR-FLOW-163 — Sidecar trace intent names the shipped argument that carries it

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | high |
| Tags | - |
| Risk | medium |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/07.doc-fact-corrections.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

When a shipped kiwi skill rendering mentions `trace_intent`, the skill text shall name on that same line an argument the shipped `add_trace_link` schema actually declares, as the carrier the value is encoded into; the full set of such lines shall be held byte-exact against a checked-in golden; and no section carrying such a line shall also carry a sentence cancelling that rule.

#### Rationale

`trace_intent` is not an argument of any MCP tool: `grep -rn "trace_intent\|traceIntent" src/` returns nothing, and `toolSchemas.add_trace_link` declares seven names that do not include it. FR-FLOW-162 settled the encoding for `kiwi-srs`, which now writes the value inside `notes`, and settled the call examples, which now all carry `relation`. What FR-FLOW-162 did not reach is the plan-to-code boundary: `kiwi-planner` declares `trace_intent` on its sidecar `TraceLink` type, the sidecar-to-flat conversion table has no row for it, and `kiwi-coder` — which owns the flattening and forbids arbitrary fields — never mentions it. So a planner-authored `addition_site` mark is dropped at the moment it becomes a real trace link, and the status cap in `kiwi-srs` §0.14, which reads `trace_intent=addition_site` out of `notes`, has no data to read for planner-authored traces.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The carrier vocabulary is the shipped schema's own. The suite reads `Object.keys(toolSchemas.add_trace_link)` out of the imported `src/mcp/server.ts` record at run time instead of restating the names, so an argument renamed or retired in code changes what the judge accepts. Measured: 7 arguments - `id`, `type`, `reference`, `relation`, `notes`, `dryRun`, `ignoreLock` (`grep -n "add_trace_link" src/mcp/server.ts` -> line 297).
- [x] AC-2: The rule refuses rather than passes when it becomes obsolete. If `toolSchemas.add_trace_link` ever declares `trace_intent` itself, encoding it into another argument is no longer required and a suite that went on approving the encoding would be approving a stale instruction; the suite fails with that reason instead. Measured now: `grep -rn "trace_intent\|traceIntent" src/` returns no line, so no shipped code reads the field under either spelling.
- [x] AC-3: Sites are derived from disk, not listed. A site is every physical line naming `trace_intent` as a WHOLE word - bounded on both sides, because measured, truncating the swept name to `trace_inten` selected the same twenty-eight lines and left every assertion green while the suite was checking a name no skill writes; with the boundaries that truncation empties the corpus and turns three axes red. The rendering list is taken from `RENDERINGS` and the file list from `markdownFiles` in `test/skills/kiwi-renderings.ts`. The swept path set is asserted equal to a fresh re-derivation from disk, so freezing today's file list into a literal fails instead of reporting a clean sweep over the survivors. Measured before this change: 20 sites, 5 in each of the four renderings.
- [x] AC-4: Every site names a carrier. A line that mentions `trace_intent` without naming any declared argument on it - backticked as `` `notes` `` or written as a key `notes:` - is reported, because it tells the reader the field exists and not where its value goes. Measured before this change: 4 violations, one per rendering, all at the sidecar `TraceLink` declaration (`skills/claude/kiwi-planner/SKILL.md:832`, `skills/codex/kiwi-planner/references/extended-workflow.md:400`, `skills/etc/kiwi-planner/references/extended-workflow.md:400`, `.agents/skills/kiwi-planner/references/extended-workflow.md:400`). After this change: 0.
- [x] AC-5: A carrier the schema does not declare is reported too. Naming `intent`, or naming `trace_intent` itself, as the destination leaves the defect exactly where it was rather than converting it into a refusal: the shape is wrapped by `objectFromShape` into `z4mini.object(...)` with no `.strict()` anywhere under `src/`, so an undeclared key is stripped and the call succeeds - measured, `{id, type, reference, relation, trace_intent: "addition_site"}` parses to the same object without `trace_intent`. A reader told to put the value in an undeclared name is told to put it somewhere it will not survive, which is the same silent loss AC-4 reports, reached by a different route. What schema validation does refuse is a MISSING REQUIRED argument such as `relation`; that is a different failure and FR-FLOW-162 settled it. The judge accepts only names present in the AC-1 fact.
- [x] AC-6: The flattening contract states the destination in every rendering, not only the skill that consumes it. `kiwi-planner` carries a `trace_intent` row in its sidecar-nested-to-MCP-flat conversion table, and `kiwi-coder`, which owns the flattening and forbids arbitrary fields, states the same destination in its flattening section. Floor buckets are keyed by rendering and skill, and the bucket set found on disk is asserted equal to the bucket set that has a floor, so a skill that loses every mention loses its bucket and fails rather than being swept past.
- [x] AC-7: The judge is exercised against known answers in both directions, with every carrier name in the samples tied to the AC-1 fact rather than typed - the accepted one taken from the declared list, the refused one asserted absent from it before use: a line naming no argument must be refused, a line naming an undeclared carrier must be refused, and a line naming a declared one must be passed. A judge rewritten into a tautology in either direction fails one of the two. Per-rendering-and-skill site floors are asserted alongside, because a reader that has stopped matching reports zero violations, which is exactly what a correct tree reports.
- [x] AC-8: The sites are frozen byte-exact against `test/skills/trace-intent-carrier.<id>.golden.md`, keyed on the file with the line number stripped so an edit above a site does not rewrite the golden. A presence check does not survive self-inversion: a line may swap the carrier for a different declared argument, or carry a sentence retracting the rule appended to the SAME line, with every token the judge reads still in place, and both are refused byte for byte. What a golden keyed on the site line does NOT reach is a retraction placed on a NEIGHBOURING line, which is AC-9's and not this one's. The golden is never written from the assertion; on mismatch the observed text is dropped beside it as `.actual` for a reader to diff.
- [x] AC-9: A rule cancelled from a line beside it is refused as well as one cancelled on it. Measured before this criterion: inserting a blank line and `다만 바로 위 문단의 인코딩 규칙은 이번 판에서 폐기하며, 참고 사항일 뿐 강제되지 않는다.` after the `kiwi-coder` site left all eight tests green, because a site is a physical line and the inserted line names no field, so neither the judge nor the byte golden sees it - and in markdown a following sentence goes on the next line more often than on the same one. Every site's enclosing section, taken from the shared `enclosingSection` so the boundary is a heading rather than a line count, is scanned for a closed retraction vocabulary assembled from the retractions this repository has measured (FR-FLOW-161, FR-FLOW-162, and the `--drive` list in `drive-mode.fr-flow-119.test.ts`, which is not imported because it guards a different subject at a different scope). The reader is exercised on four samples with known answers: a cancellation below the site and one above it are refused, a section that only states the rule is passed, and a cancellation in the NEXT section is passed, which pins the boundary rather than endorsing it. Measured on this tree: 28 sites, 1275 section lines scanned, 0 reports. Widening the golden to that span instead of scanning it was priced and refused - those lines carry `kiwi-srs` §0's 25-row policy table, the whole sidecar-to-flat conversion table and the `McpCall` interface, all owned by other requirements, which is the cost FR-FLOW-155 measured for whole-section freezing and FR-FLOW-161 cited when it froze rule lines only.
- [x] AC-10: The suite refuses its own quiet disablement, for the three edits measured to survive it. (a) The golden comparison takes the golden's READER rather than its text and derives the other side itself, so the assertion has no argument to re-point; measured, with the comparison written inline as `expect(actual).toBe(golden)`, changing `golden` to `actual` left all eight tests green and hid a swapped carrier completely. Three samples with known answers exercise it - an identical golden passes, an empty one and one whose first site names a different field are refused - so a comparison neutered inside the function fails two of the three. (b) The criteria this file owes a block to are listed and asserted against the `it` titles read off the file's own source, bounded on the right so `AC-1` is not answered by `AC-10`; measured, deleting the AC-8 block left seven tests green with a lower count as the only trace, and it is now reported by name. `describe` titles are not counted, because a `describe` runs nothing. (c) The floor table's TOTAL is asserted against the recorded census of 28, because a floor only refuses zero: measured, lowering one skill's floor from 4 to 1 left all eight tests green.
- [x] AC-11: What this requirement does not guarantee, each measured rather than inferred. (a) The judge accepts any declared argument on the line, including one present for an unrelated reason - deleting the destination sentence from `kiwi-srs` §0.14 while leaving its `id` · `type` · `reference` · `relation` enumeration in place passed it, and 8 of the 28 sites are of that shape; only the golden reports them. (b) AC-9's vocabulary closes spellings, not the subject: a paraphrase carrying none of its phrases is not reached, which is the residual FR-FLOW-155 AC-4 records for the same device, and neither is a cancellation placed in a neighbouring section. (c) The corpus equality cannot see a frozen file list on the day it is frozen; it turns red the next time a markdown file is added or removed. (d) A coordinated edit that changes a site and the golden together still lands. (e) The block-set assertion in AC-10 cannot report its own deletion. (f) This reads instruction text: a skill carrying the corrected line and an agent ignoring it are not distinguished, and whether `kiwi-srs` actually enforces the `addition_site` status cap is not checked here.

### FR-FLOW-164 — The chain that promotes declares the gate that stops on a validation error, and the helper that reads gate tables finds a declaration by its heading

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | functional |
| Target | 3.1.0 |
| Status | verified |
| Priority | critical |
| Tags | plan-3.0-18, audit-28 |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | docs/plan/3.0/18.validate-spec-error-wiring.md, docs/research/28.skills-mcp-end-to-end-audit.md |

#### Requirement

The shared helper that locates a skill's `critical_gates[]` declaration SHALL find it by the heading that names `critical_gates`, not by one skill's section number, so that `criticalGateRows()` returns the declared rows for each of the seven chain skills this requirement names rather than only for the two whose declaration happens to sit under `## 0.G`. The seven skills of the implementation, review and promotion chain — `kiwi-orchestrator`, `kiwi-wave-master`, `kiwi-review-fix-loop`, `kiwi-pm`, `kiwi-coder`, `kiwi-tdd` and `kiwi-planner` — SHALL each declare `validate-spec-error` in that table, in every rendering they ship, with a reason and a location. The declaring section SHALL also state where the gate is observed: the validation call to run, the hop it runs before, and the halt on an error-severity diagnostic regardless of `--auto`. A row without that statement is a gate identifier with nothing behind it, which `kiwi-orchestrator` §0.G already calls worse than an omission. The identifier SHALL be a member of the exported `GATE_IDS` union, because the cross-variant parity assertion runs `declared ⊆ union` and would otherwise fail the harness on correct skill text.

#### Rationale

The audit (docs/research/28 §3.7) measured that exactly one skill stops on a validation error, `kiwi-srs-sync`, and it sits outside the chain that implements, reviews and promotes. The seven skills that do implement, review and promote declare the gate zero times, so an SRS carrying error-severity diagnostics does not stop any of them; under `--auto` an undeclared gate falls to `business-decision`, which a committee auto-approves at confidence at or above 0.7, and the stop is silent. The audit also drew the distinction this requirement turns on: `kiwi-orchestrator` does run `speckiwi validate` at wave close, but the gate consuming that run keys on index drift, so whether an `SRS-E005` block-metadata error stops the run is left to the agent's reading. What runs and what the verdict reads are two different things. Fixing the declaration alone was not possible: `criticalGateRows()` searched for `^##\s*0\.G\b`, which two of the seven carry and five do not, so a test written over the seven would have been permanently red or would have forced a re-numbering of fifteen files. This requirement is the C and D that item 04 carried and its committee split out.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: `criticalGatesSection()` locates a declaration by the heading that names `critical_gates` rather than by the literal `## 0.G`, and `criticalGateRows()` therefore returns rows for every skill in the chain. Measured at `946b5c2`, where the working tree was byte-identical to HEAD for all 27 shipped files this touches: the old rule `^##\s*0\.G\b` returned 58 rows for `kiwi-orchestrator` in each of the four trees, 18 for `kiwi-wave-master` in each of the three it ships, and 0 for `kiwi-review-fix-loop`, `kiwi-pm`, `kiwi-coder`, `kiwi-tdd` and `kiwi-planner` in every tree. The new rule returns the same 58 and the same 18 — the generalization is a no-op for the two skills whose heading was already `## 0.G`, which is what proves it did not move the denominator of the three suites that already read this helper — and 14, 13, 15, 3 and 6 for the five that returned nothing. Those before-counts cannot be re-derived once the old rule is gone, so they are recorded here; the live assertion is a per-pair floor over pairs derived from disk, and a pair returning zero fails naming its file. A second live assertion covers what a floor of one cannot: for each skill the sorted set of declared gate ids is identical across every rendering that ships it, so a row added to one rendering and not the others fails at the set rather than at the count. The heading rule misses three sites, named so the limit is measured: `skills/claude/kiwi-commit-auto-pr/SKILL.md` (§14.9), `skills/claude/kiwi-commit-auto-push/SKILL.md` (§11.10) and `skills/claude/kiwi-srs-sync/SKILL.md` (§0.16, inline in a cell) declare under headings that omit the token, which `auto-option.md` §5.0.1 allows; the codex, etc and mirror renderings of those skills are reached, so this is three sites, not skills. A SET EQUALITY over every kiwi skill of every rendering holds it: the sites naming `critical_gates` with no rows are exactly those three paths, read out of this text — so a fourth fails, as does one becoming reachable.
- [x] AC-2: Each of the seven skills named in the Requirement declares `validate-spec-error` as a row of its `critical_gates[]` table, with a non-empty reason and a non-empty location, in `skills/claude`, `skills/codex` and `skills/etc`, and in `.agents/skills` for the six that are mirrored. The seven names are read out of the Requirement statement by the suite rather than listed in the test file; the identifier itself is derived from that same statement as the single backticked lower-kebab token that is not one of those skill names, and is separately asserted to be a `GATE_IDS` member by AC-4 — derived that way rather than from the union, because a derivation that read the union would make AC-4 answer itself. The renderings and the mirror exclusion are read from disk, so narrowing the swept set is a requirement diff or a tree change rather than a test-file edit. Two floors are named here and read out of this text by the suite, so removing a name from the Requirement fails a count as well as shrinking a sweep: `chain 7` and `sites 27`. Baseline: `validate-spec-error` stood in exactly four shipped files before this change, all four of them `kiwi-srs-sync`, and in none of the seven — reproduced with `grep -rl validate-spec-error skills/ .agents/skills/`.
- [x] AC-3: The declaring section states where the gate is observed, so the row is not an identifier with nothing behind it. Each of the 27 sections carries a PROSE line — table rows excluded, since the row's own reason cell names the call and counting it would let the sentence be deleted while the count stayed at one — naming the MCP tool `validate_spec`, the CLI fallback `speckiwi validate`, the identifier `validate-spec-error` and `--auto`, and saying that an error-severity diagnostic stops the hop this row's third cell names regardless of `--auto`. The four tokens are read out of the clause above by the suite rather than typed into the test file, so loosening `speckiwi validate` to `speckiwi` is a requirement diff rather than a test-file edit; the identifier that clause yields is asserted equal to the one AC-2 derives from the Requirement statement, so the two derivations answer each other rather than each standing alone.
